Add a splash of gravity-defying fun to your day with this charming Penguin Roly-Poly Toy! Designed as a self-righting wobble toy, this penguin tumbles, rocks, and spins for 30+ seconds before standing right back up again. This innovative toy combines simple physics with playful interaction, creating a fun hands-on experience for all ages while also encouraging curiosity and exploration! 🧠 The Educational Aspect: Learning Through Play This toy introduces core concepts through interactive play: Cause & Effect: Early learners discover that their physical actions (a tap or push) create immediate reactions. Motor Skills: Following the 30+ second wobble improves visual tracking, while reaching for it refines hand-eye coordination. Introduction to Physics: The self-righting action naturally introduces older kids to center of gravity, balance, and momentum, sparking curiosity about how things work. ⚙️ Technical Features & Design Built to be an elegant, easy-to-print project, this model maximizes performance without relying on external parts: Enduring Motion: Precisely calibrated geometry ensures a single push creates a sustained wobble lasting over 30 seconds. Zero Hardware Required: Unlike traditional designs that need metal bearings or screws, this relies entirely on its 3D-printed structure and solid infill to self-right. Accessible Printing (NO AMS Needed): A smart multipart design lets you print different colors on separate plates for a multi-color look. A rapid single-color version is also included. Streamlined Assembly: Intuitive tolerances allow pieces to fit together smoothly, requiring only a small drop of adhesive for a highly durable bond. 🛠️ Step-by-Step Assembly Guide The assembly process is straightforward and consists of 6 simple steps . For the best results, having some CA glue (superglue) on hand is recommended. Step 1: Clean the Prints Carefully remove all support material from the printed parts. Ensure all mating surfaces are clean and smooth for a flush fit. Step 2: Install the Base Connectors Insert all four alignment connectors into the base. Because this model is subject to constant kinetic movement, it is highly recommended to apply a small amount of CA glue in a cross-shape between the connectors to lock them securely. Step 3: Secure the Body Align both components of the body and press the pieces firmly together, holding them in place until the glue has fully set. Step 4: Assemble the Face Details Insert the two eyes into the designated slots on the white belly piece . This may require some force, as they are designed to stay in place without using glue. Step 5: Fit the Belly Panel Press the completed belly and eye assembly directly into the front cutout of the penguin's body. This part is designed for a precise friction-fit and does not require any extra glue . Step 6: Attach the Beak For the final step, add a small drop of glue to the back of the penguin's beak and push it into the face cutout. Kumiko Edition Rubik's Cube: Fully 3D Printed Classic mechanical puzzles meet traditional Japanese woodworking aesthetics. I wanted to design a fully functional Rubik's Cube that looks like a piece of art on your desk, but more importantly, I wanted to eliminate the need for any non-printed parts. Key Features Intricate Kumiko Aesthetics: The faces feature a beautifully detailed lattice pattern inspired by traditional Japanese craftsmanship. No Hardware Needed: No screws, springs, or glue. The entire mechanism is designed to be printed. Print-in-Place Hinged Caps: The centre caps feature a built-in hinge. Once threaded onto the core, this allows the outer faces of the cube to rotate freely and smoothly. Reinforced Threaded Core: The custom-designed central cross is engineered to provide multi-directional strength, holding everything securely in place. Assembly Guide This cube is designed for satisfying, mechanical assembly. Here is the step-by-step breakdown: Construct the Core: Thread the centre caps onto the central cross, give the caps a little wiggle whilst tightening to help separate the print in place hinge. If the caps are too tight and wont separate, use some pliers to secure the stem whilst turning the cap. The Bottom Layer: Place the four bottom edge pieces around the bottom centre cap, followed by the bottom corner pieces. The Middle Layer: Slot the middle edge pieces into place. Tip: Rotate the bottom tier slightly to make sliding these middle edges in much easier. The Top Layer: When placing the top corners and edges, rotate the top face 45° . for the clearance to drop the pieces into place. The Final Piece: Leave one top edge piece for last. Angle the bottom of the piece into the track and press it down and in with some force until it snaps securely into place, Printability Because this model features functioning mechanical threads and intricate surface patterns, precision is key. Materials Used: Bambu PLA Wood, PLA-CF, Matte PLA & PLA Basic Orientation & Supports: To achieve the highest quality finish on the Kumiko lattice, the pieces are now oriented to print face up . Important Support Advice: If you are printing with a single material and are not using a dedicated support filament for the interface, please revert the support settings to default . Otherwise, the supports will fuse to your model and be incredibly difficult to remove! Layer Height: 0.16mm is recommended (as set in the print profile). This finer resolution ensures the threaded core screws together smoothly and the delicate Kumiko lines print cleanly.

description: 大家好！此模型是來自 IDW 《Transformers / Back to the Future》 聯名漫畫裡可變成滑板的變形金剛 Skilz ，因為官方一直沒有推出能搭配時光車 Gigawatt 比例的實體玩具，於是自己嘗試建模設計了一款。由於這只是個人設計的業餘作品，可能沒辦法像官方玩具那麼完善，但基本的變形功能以及可動關節都有做出來，分享給同樣喜歡這個角色的朋友！ 模型是採用單色列印，後續再上色的模式，因為零件細小，用AMS分色列印效果可能不佳。 模型基本設計： 【嘗試完全變形】：設計上可從機器人模式變形為滑板模式，不需要拆卸零件，但也可拆下部分零件做為原創武器，讓整體比例更協調。 【配合 Gigawatt 比例】：機器人模式的尺寸是有特別與官方的時光車 Gigawatt 進行調整，放在一起的比例感還算合適。 【可動關節與支架】：模型具備基本的可動關節可調整姿勢，背後也附上直徑3mm的插孔安裝通用支架，可有不同的展示方式。 ⚠️ 一些列印與組裝的提醒： 【0.2噴嘴與0.4噴嘴】：使用0.2噴嘴搭配0.06層高可達到最佳列印品質，若使用0.4噴嘴則需搭配0.08層高，但零件可能出現小瑕疵需要額外修整。 【線材與底板清潔】：建議使用已烘乾的PLA進行列印，列印前適當清潔底板確保過程中零件不位移。 【分盤列印】：因為零件數量不少且細小，因此把零件做成框架的模式進行列印。建議按照檔案內的安排分盤列印，確保較高的成功率與品質。 【細節與公差】：零件尺寸較小，列印後關節處或插銷插孔的位置可能需要自行修剪，或是用筆刀微調才能更順利組裝與變形。 【支撐與底板接觸面】：在拆除支撐時須注意有完整拆除，若有殘留可能會影響組裝，會有過緊甚至是損壞零件的可能。零件與底板接觸面的部分需注意是否有毛邊，這部分也可能會影響組裝。 【懸空處修整】：部分懸空處可不用加上支撐，但需要處理垂下的耗材，避免影響組裝。 各框架列印完成冷卻後，可直接由此處提起，把零件從底板上一次分離。 以下是詳細的組裝步驟： 1. 身體部分以側向90度的方向插入後再轉正即可，若過緊可能是球關節上有毛邊需稍微修整。 2. 大腿部分直接按壓裝入即可，可放在桌面上施力會比較輕鬆。須注意左右零件不同。 3. 小腿安裝左右腿對稱，零件插槽可先安裝測試完鬆緊度再把C扣扣上。 4. 肩關節可由約45度角的方向壓入，安裝上臂時請小心肩關節滑動，上臂零件可放在桌面上再壓入會比較容易施力。 5. 手臂C扣較脆弱，安裝前須注意零件狀態是否需要修整。 6. 頭部以側向90度方向插入，再轉正即可。 7. 背後插孔部分若無支撐，可能會有一些懸垂的耗材需要移除。小翅膀轉軸上有支撐需要移除，請確保有確實移除乾淨，不然可能會損壞背後的卡槽。安裝時建議由側向卡入後再進行旋轉，第一次旋轉時須注意不要讓轉軸滑出卡槽。 8. 腳部的第一次變形，由於零件細小，在把零件從插槽拔出時須注意力道，可藉由旋轉腳掌零件讓收納過程不會有零件干涉。完成後腳掌零件與小腿間有卡扣可固定。 這算是一個還在實驗與優化階段的嘗試，稱不上是非常成熟的模型。大家如果有任何修改建議， 非常歡迎在下方留言討論 ，謝謝大家！

Also watch your fingers to avoid getting them pinched. Use at your own ris k. This bottle opener is not a decoration — it’s a functional tool that has to handle force when opening a bottle. That’s why the following points are important to make sure it works properly. The opener has to fit the bottle exactly. Only when it sits correctly can it apply the necessary force without damaging itself. You can find out how to identify the correct bottle shape in the instructions . Additionally, using the right filament is crucial. Filaments with additives like silk, matte, wood, or similar effects tend to make the print more brittle and less durable , so the bottle opener could break more easily. Even PLA-CF and PETG-CF can be more brittle because of the added fibers. For the best results, regular standard filaments are recommended . A clear recommendation for the opener base is regular PLA , since it offers high stiffness , barely bends, and is sufficiently durable. This helps maintain an exact fit, even while opening the bottle. PETG works as well, but it’s a lot less stiff and flexes more under pressure. In the worst case, the lever can slip off and get damaged by the bottle cap without even opening the bottle. If you want to use more advanced filaments, I assume you already know how to work with them. There are also plenty of other factors that can vary, like the filament brand, bottle manufacturer, drink temperature, printing process, how the opener is used, and more . TrayStack ist ein kompakter Organizer für Kleinteile, Werkzeuge oder SD-Karten, der speziell für den Schreibtisch entwickelt wurde. Das gesamte System ist auf den Bauraum des A1 mini optimiert, liefert maximale Stabilität bei minimalem Materialeinsatz und folgt dem Prinzip: Form Follows Function . Vergleich zwischen dem TrayStack Desktop Organizer (links) und dem TrayStack MAX System (rechts) Darf es auch etwas größer sein? Nutzt gern das neue TrayStack MAX System um wirklich alles perfekt zu verstauen. Hier geht es zum TrayStack MAX System Das Konzept: Drei Ebenen. Ein Griff. Volle Kontrolle. Das System besteht aus einer Außenbox und drei perfekt abgestimmten Einsätzen: Der Base-Tray (Unten): Verfügt über einen integrierten Zentralgriff, der über die gesamte Höhe des Systems ragt. Er bildet die stabile "Wirbelsäule". Die Stack-Trays (Mitte & Oben): Dank präzise tolerierter Führungsschlitze werden die oberen Schalen einfach über den Griff gefädelt und gleiten ruckelfrei in Position. Das Handling: Wenn alle Einsätze ineinandergesteckt sind, greifst du einfach den zentralen Griff und hebst den kompletten 3-stöckigen Block mit einer Hand aus der Box oder setzt ihn wieder ein. Kein Wackeln, kein Verkanten. Volle Flexibilität: 4 Varianten pro Ebene Um das Maximum an Individualität für dein Setup herauszuholen, ist das System komplett modular aufgebaut. Jeder einzelne Einsatz (Base, Mittelteil und Oberteil) existiert in 4 verschiedenen Varianten mit unterschiedlichen Tray-Größen und Fächereinteilungen. Diese wählst du dir einfach über die Plattenauswahl des entsprechenden Druckprofils aus. Egal ob du lange Stifte, winzige SMD-Bauteile, Schrauben, USB-Sticks oder Werkzeug verstauen willst - du kannst dir genau die Kombination ausdrucken, die du für deinen Workflow brauchst. Bewusste Design-Entscheidung: Keine vertikale Stapelbarkeit Ein wichtiger Hinweis zur Design-Philosophie dieses Projekts: Die Boxen sind bewusst NICHT vertikal in die Höhe stapelbar designt. Warum? Um das klare, minimalistische und funktionale Design auf dem Schreibtisch zu erhalten. Vertikale Stapelsysteme neigen bei dieser kompakten Grundfläche dazu, klobig zu wirken und den schnellen Zugriff zu blockieren. TrayStack setzt auf direkten, ergonomischen Workflow auf einer Ebene. Modulare Erweiterung: Das TrayStack Grid Du brauchst mehr Platz? Statt in die Höhe zu bauen, erweitert sich TrayStack in der Ebene. Über das TrayStack Grid kannst du das System der Länge nach modular erweitern. Mit dem Grid lassen sich mehrere Boxen nahtlos und bombenfest nebeneinander fixieren. So wächst dein Organizer-System exakt mit deinen Anforderungen, während dein Schreibtisch optisch clean und aufgeräumt bleibt. Für maximale Flexibilität beim Drucken stehen dir 3 verschiedene Grid-Komponenten zur Verfügung: Das Single-Grid: Perfekt, wenn du eine einzelne, isolierte Box sauber einfassen und ihr einen festen Stand auf dem Tisch verpassen willst. Das End-Piece (Außenseite): Der Abschluss-Gris für die Außenseitem. Wenn du exakt zwei Boxen nebeneinander nutzen willst, druckst du einfach nur zwei Stück davon. Sie werden direkt miteinander verbunden, und du kannst deine zwei Boxen hineinstellen. Das Extension-Piece (Verlängerungsteil): Das universelle Mittelstück. Hiermit kannst du deine Reihe in der Mitte beliebig oft und unendlich erweitern, um so viele Boxen nebeneinander zu stellen, wie dein Schreibtisch hergibt.

Feedback from makes and testing will help shape future improved versions of the design. Jellyfish Wind Spinner Bring kinetic ocean-inspired motion into your garden with this fully 3D printable wind spinner designed to mimic the flowing movement of a jellyfish swimming through water. Unlike traditional front-facing fan-style wind spinners, this design uses a circular array of sideways propeller segments that continuously fold inward and expand outward while spinning, creating a mesmerizing overlapping motion effect from every angle. The spinner is built from 14 interconnected blade segments, each carefully dimensioned and positioned to maximize movement while preventing unwanted interference between parts during rotation. The result is a hypnotic and almost alien-looking form that appears alive in strong wind conditions. What Makes This Design Unique Most wind spinners rely on a simple forward-facing turbine or spiral design. This model instead uses a ring of sideways-facing propeller elements that catch wind from virtually any orientation. Carefully positioned aerodynamic “cups” on each segment help direct airflow efficiently into the rotating structure, allowing the spinner to move with smooth repeating motion across its full circular form. Image 1 shows the “carefully positioned aerodynamic cups” of the model. Image 2 shows a section analysis (in Fusion 360) of the internal geometry of the model, allowing it to print as two locked-together parts while still being freely able to spin around. Image 3 shows a print-optimized hinge with a built-in locking mechanism (the “clicking part” of the segment). Each propeller segment rotates around a section of the outer frame using a custom low-friction printed mechanism (image 2) designed specifically for FDM printing. Multiple prototype iterations were required to achieve the final balance between: rotational freedom, print reliability, structural strength, and assembly stability. The geometry was also engineered with internal reinforcement features that intentionally generate additional wall lines in slicers at critical stress points and weak areas, increasing durability without adding unnecessary bulk. This project was heavily inspired by the organic underwater movement of a jellyfish, resulting in a shape that feels: organic, futuristic, floral, hypnotic, and slightly alien. Printing Information Recommended Settings Material: PLA recommended Supports: Only required for the stand Layer Height: 0.2 mm recommended Glue: Not required AMS Compatible: Yes Fully 3D printable No additional hardware required Printer Compatibility The propeller segments can be printed: 2 at a time on Bambu Lab P/X/A1 printers 1 at a time on A1 Mini (The A1 Mini canot print the stand) 3–4 at a time on larger H-series machines Approximate print time: ~2.5 hours per pair of segments depending on settings Assembly Instructions The assembly process follows the included visual guide. Step 1 – Print the Stand Begin by printing the ground stand/base for the spinner. Step 2 – Install the Propeller Segments Each sideways propeller segment attaches to the next using the same twist-lock mechanism: Insert the stud with the small overhang into the rear opening of the neighboring segment Twist until aligned as shown in the assembly images Connect the protruding rod into the locking holder of the adjacent segment Flex the holder gently over the rod until it clicks into place This connection system ensures all propeller positions remain properly aligned around the circular frame. Here is a video of step 2: Step 3 – Close the Final Segment Once all segments are connected, the final section slides into the original stand connection point to complete the full ring structure. No glue is required for normal assembly, though glue can optionally be added for increased durability in extreme outdoor wind conditions. Wind Performance This spinner is optimized for moderate to strong wind conditions and performs best outdoors in open airflow environments such as: gardens, balconies, patios, or outdoor kinetic art displays. In lower wind conditions the structure may require STRONGER AIRFLOW TO ACHIEVE FULL ROTATIONAL MOTION due to friction from the complex interconnected geometry. Design Journey This project went through many iterations before reaching the final result. Nearly every mechanism was redesigned multiple times to balance: smooth movement, structural strength, printability, and assembly simplicity. What began as a difficult concept sketch slowly evolved into a fully functional kinetic sculpture built entirely for FDM printing. One of my favorite parts of this project is that when I first showed the original concept sketches to a friend, he laughed and told me it would never be possible to make something like this on a 3D printer. That challenge became a huge source of motivation throughout the design process and I think it is safe to say he was wrong. This design was incredibly fun to develop, and I may revisit it in the future with additional improvements or alternative mounting systems for different display options. description: Hey there! :) At first, I wanted to just design a detailed human spine as an earcuff earring. But then I tested the first prototype, and I really didn't like how.. plain it looked. So I had this brilliant idea of going in a mythical direction and turning it into a little floating winged body on your ear instead. You know, like the little angel that appears on your shoulder and tells you to do or not to do certain stuff. What does it tell you? Well, it depends on which ear you decide to wear it! :D So, like my two previous earcuff holeless earrings, my goals for this design were comfort, stability, and being cool. :D However, I learned from your comments under the previous designs and did my best to modify the design to make the support removal easier. Also, I further tuned the print profile to give you clean surfaces and low-hassle supports that break away easily. Sizing: The uploaded profile that fits me best is about 10 cm in the Y direction. To go one size up, select all components and scale them up by about 10%. Use 10% increments to scale it up more. Print Notes (For anyone who's not using the profile I've uploaded): 0.12 or 0.16 mm layer heights, 2 walls & 0% infill (to make your print stronger, you can increase the number of walls, but it will make your earring heavier). Change the Seam Position to “Nearest” . For a better surface quality, you'll need to lower your printing speed quite a lot. I've uploaded this profile with a 90 mm/s wall-printing speed, but I suggest going even lower, to about 60 or 50 mm/s if your printer isn't a Bambulab. Enable outer brims generation. Support Tuning (For anyone who's not using the profile I've uploaded): This is a rather support-intensive design, and for that reason, we need trustworthy supports that won't fail, but also break away easily and leave the final surface undamaged and as smooth as possible. Here's how I tuned the profile for that: Lower the threshold to about 20 or 25 degrees. Increase the initial support expansion to 5 mm. Increase the support wall loops to 2. Increase the support/object gap to about 0.28 mm. Change the Interface Pattern to “Rectilinear”. Esta es mi versión del Pentaclick , basada en el modelo original pero con varias modificaciones orientadas a mejorar el diseño a mi gusto. He rediseñado todas las piezas: la tapa ahora permite ver el pentágono completo y oculta los enganches; las caras tienen un acabado más redondeado ; y el soporte de las gomas se ha ajustado, ampliando ligeramente el hueco para la goma y reduciendo la zona de apoyo, con el objetivo de disminuir el roce y evitar que las gomas se desgasten en exceso. Debido a estas modificaciones, el modelo no puede imprimirse montado y es necesario imprimir cada pieza por separado. Aunque esto puede parecer un pequeño inconveniente, también ofrece la ventaja de poder personalizar los colores de cada pieza y combinarlos al gusto. Además, este diseño evita que el mecanismo se quede en posición “aplastada” tras hacer clic. Está hecho así intencionadamente, aunque puede considerarse un cambio respecto al comportamiento del modelo original. Para su funcionamiento es necesario utilizar una goma elástica. Recomiendo usar gomas pequeñas de pelo o las típicas de hacer pulseras; cuanto más finas sean, mejor resultado dan y más durarán, ya que las gomas más gruesas tienden a desgastarse antes. (también, según algún comentario sriben las gomas de las ortodoncias) El montaje se realiza pieza a pieza siguiendo la siguiente secuencia: El primer paso puede ser el más complicado: encajar el soporte de la goma con las caras. Puedes ayudarte apoyando la pieza sobre una mesa y presionando el lateral contra el soporte para facilitar el ajuste. Esto suele ocurrir porque la pieza puede imprimirse ligeramente más grande debido a pequeñas variaciones en el comportamiento del material utilizado. En mis pruebas, las mejores tolerancias las he conseguido utilizando PLA Mate de Bambu Lab. Asegúrate de colocar en la dirección correcta los soportes de las gomas como en la imagen con la ranura en la dirección de la cara exterior. Introducing the Customisable Skadis Bin Generator Standard storage bins rarely accommodate the exact dimensions of our tools and components, often leading to wasted space or awkwardly crammed hardware on our IKEA Skådis pegboards. Whether you are managing an electronics workbench, sorting precision fasteners, or organising heavy crafting tools, off-the-shelf solutions simply do not offer the granular control required for a truly optimised workspace. To resolve this, I have engineered the Flat-Pack Skådis Bin Generator. Generating Your Bespoke Bin Accessing the generator is straightforward using MakerWorld’s built-in Parametric Model Maker. Instead of downloading a static file, click the green "Customize" button at the top of the model page. On mobile select the “Prepare to Print” button then select the green "Customise model" Within the parameters panel on the left side of the interface, you can tailor the bin exactly to your requirements: Width & Height: Adjusted in 40mm increments to perfectly align with the standard Skådis grid system. Depth: Scalable in 10mm increments to accommodate anything from shallow trays for SD cards to deep bins for hand tools. Lattice vs. Solid: Toggle the Lattice parameter (1 for on, 0 for off) to switch between a lightweight, visible-contents design and a solid structural panel. Inserts & Dividers: Enable custom internal inserts (1) and specify the exact number of Dividers you need to keep your small parts segregated. Once configured, simply hit the blue "Generate" button to preview your model, followed by "Download" to export your unique files for slicing. Key Benefits Massive Parametric Sizing: Generate dimensions ranging from 80x60x80mm up to 320x240x160mm. Custom Divider Inserts: Automatically generate drop-in inserts tailored to your specific bin dimensions, ensuring hardware remains rigorously sorted. Flat-Pack Assembly: The individual panels print flat for maximum strength and bed adhesion and slot together via engineered joints to create a highly rigid final structure. Support-Free Geometry: Print cleanly without the need for support material, saving filament and post-processing time. Interchangeable Aesthetics: Swap between solid panels for a clean look or a lattice frame to quickly identify contents. Technical Printability I typically run these in Sunlu PLA+ or standard PETG for enhanced impact resistance. Given the flat-pack nature of the design, an optimal first layer is paramount. Structural Integrity: For robust joints that will withstand heavy, continuous loading, bump your wall loops to 3 or 4. This is far more effective for overall strength than simply increasing infill density. A 15% infill is perfectly adequate for the internal panel structures. Bed Adhesion: Because the panels print entirely flat against the build plate, they rely heavily on excellent bed adhesion to prevent warping at the corners. Ensure your plate is thoroughly cleaned and degreased before starting a batch. Supports: The geometry is fully optimised for support-free printing. Ensure your cooling is dialled in to handle the bridging sections on the panels and Insert. Conclusion Stop settling for standard, one-size-fits-all storage. With the new Flat-Pack Skadis Bin Generator, you are in complete control of your organisation system. Mix and match colours, divide your spaces, and build the ultimate pegboard setup.

Dieses modulare Pinzettensystem wurde für den Modellbau, Elektronikarbeiten und filigrane Montageaufgaben entwickelt. Das Design trennt den federnden Pinzettengriff von den funktionellen Spitzen. Dadurch wird eine hohe Flexibilität im Einsatz erreicht, während gleichzeitig der Materialaufwand auf ein Minimum reduziert wird. Die Pinzetten sind so konstruiert, dass der ideale Druckpunkt auf dem Grip liegt (die 3 schrägen Striche). Bitte lasst den Druck komplett abkühlen, um eventuelles Warping zu vermeiden. Der Nutzer Brandero hat freundlicherweise ein YouTube-Short über unsere Pinzette erstellt, was wir euch natürlich nicht vorenthalten möchten: Funktionsprinzip und Mechanik Die Montage der verschiedenen Spitzen erfolgt über eine form- und kraftschlüssige Arretierung. Die Montage ist am Anfang etwas schwergängig - das ist ganz normal. Bei Verschleiß der Spitzen muss nicht das gesamte Werkzeug, sondern ausschließlich das betroffene Spitzen-Paar getauscht werden. Kompatible Spitzen-Geometrien Das System umfasst fünf spezialisierte Spitzen-Varianten, die je nach Anforderungsszenario werkzeuglos gewechselt werden: Schaufel-Spitze: Bietet eine maximale Auflagefläche zum flächigen Untergreifen und Heben extrem flacher Bauteile wie Folien, Aufkleber oder SMD-Komponenten, ohne punktuellen Druck auszuüben. Präzisions-Keilspitze: Läuft linear und symmetrisch spitz zu, um feinste Positionierungsarbeiten in engen Zwischenräumen oder das Halten minimaler zylindrischer Objekte zu ermöglichen. Stumpfe Flachspitze: Eine universelle, rechteckige Greiffläche mit definierter Kante, die die Haltekraft homogen über die gesamte Breite verteilt und optimalen Grip für quaderförmige Kleinteile bietet. Abgewinkelte Keilspitze: Eine anatomisch abgewinkelte Geometrie für ergonomisches Arbeiten, die dem Anwender eine freie vertikale Sicht auf das Bauteil erlaubt, während die Hand in einer natürlichen Haltung bleibt. Hakenspitze: Eine stark gebogene 90°-Hakenspitze für verwinkelte Areale, ausgelegt zum Untergreifen von Hindernissen oder zum Hochziehen von Drähten bei blockiertem vertikalem Zugang. Jetzt auch mit Aufbewahrungsbox Da es einige Nachfragen nach einer Aufbewahrungsbox gab, haben wir noch eine für Euch erstellt :-) Darin ist neben dem Platz für Pinzettengriff und Wechselspitzen auch noch etwas Raum für Kleinteile wie Magnete etc. Übrigens: Der Deckel ist von uns bewusst “gleitend” konstruiert, weil das Set bei uns auf dem Schreibtisch steht. Den Griff zum herausziehen haben wir bei bei diesem Modell etwas außerhalb der Mitte platziert, um noch genügend Platz für das größere Kleinteile-Fach zu haben.

Canard Glider – Experimental Series #1 This model is the first design in my Experimental Series , where I explore unconventional aircraft concepts and flight characteristics. Inspired by aircraft designer, Burt Rutan’s Long-EZ, this glider uses a canard configuration , meaning the front wing provides both lift and pitch control—very different from a traditional layout. Features Canard layout (front wing acts as elevator + lift) Cambered main wing for efficient glide Dihedral wing for added stability Winglets for improved lateral control Clean, lightweight design Flight Performance Flies very straight and stable Capable of long, smooth glides Handles strong hand launches without stalling Easy to gain height with a firm throw I recommend checking out the complete lineup and save your favorites for later. Complete Lineup Cumulus 680 — slow, smooth, relaxed glides Cumulus 400 Speed Wing — faster flights Stratus 500 — balanced and versatile Stratus 500 A1 mini version - Original size Assembly guide: 1) Winglets: Align slot on winglet and wing and slide the winglet fully on. 2) Canard : Place the canard inside hole and insert pins into holes. Lock the canard in place by inserting the canard lock into the slot: 3) Main wings: Insert wings into the slots in the fuselage. then press the clamps into the designated grooves to secure them. Note the clamp orientation. Your glider is now fully assembled and ready to fly! I wish you a happy flight :) In the following text post I wanted to give interested makers a closer look into the development process behind the Canard Glider that I submitted for the Spring Play Challenge contest. Inspiration The Canard Glider was heavily inspired by Burt Rutan’s experimental aircraft, especially the iconic Long-EZ configuration. My goal was to create a compact and highly printable glider that combined stable flight characteristics with the distinctive appearance of a real canard aircraft. Special attention was given to preserving the recognizable silhouette and canopy shape of the original aircraft while still optimizing the design for lightweight printing and stable glide performance. Iterative Development The project went through many iterations during development. I continuously experimented with: canard geometry wing camber dihedral center of gravity canard incidence angle structural reinforcement Even very small changes produced surprisingly large differences in flight behavior. Although the canard variations above appear visually similar, each configuration produced different flight characteristics. Some versions created unstable flight with excessive wing rocking, while heavier versions introduced too much nose-down pitching behavior. The final configuration was selected because it produced the smoothest and most stable glide while still maintaining enough lift and pitch recovery. Stability and Center of Gravity One of the biggest challenges was balancing the aircraft correctly. Canard aircraft require a much more forward center of gravity than conventional gliders, and small weight changes had major effects on stability. Material was intentionally removed from the upper parts of the fuselage and canard structure in order to move the center of gravity lower inside the aircraft body. This improved roll stability and reduced unwanted rocking during glide. The lightweight truss-like fuselage structure therefore serves multiple purposes: reducing weight improving stiffness lowering the center of gravity and maintaining printability. Canard Aerodynamics The final canard configuration uses approximately 3 degrees of positive incidence relative to the main wing. This allows the canard to generate lift early while also improving pitch stability and self-correcting flight behavior. The red markings indicate the canard root angle, while the blue markings indicate the main wing root angle. A major goal was ensuring that the canard stalls before the main wing. This causes the aircraft to naturally lower its nose and recover instead of entering a deeper stall. The final geometry provided the best balance between: smooth glide performance forgiving launches stable recovery behavior and reliable flight characteristics. One advantage of the canard configuration is that the aircraft remains stable even during aggressive launches, making it easier for both children and adults to fly successfully. Structural Design The canard leading edge was reinforced because it experiences the highest landing loads. The reinforcement also helped move more weight toward the front of the aircraft, which became important for achieving the correct balance. Throughout development I continuously balanced: structural stiffness weight distribution aerodynamic efficiency and printability. Future Development One maker suggested experimenting with a powered version of the aircraft. I happened to have a small motor, capacitor, and charging circuit available, so I decided to test a lightweight electric configuration. Surprisingly, the concept worked remarkably well and opened up interesting possibilities for future development. The powered version still preserves much of the original canard stability and flight behavior, and it will likely become part of future iterations. Final Goal The final objective of the project was not simply to create another printable glider, but to develop an aircraft that combined: experimental aviation aesthetics aerodynamic exploration reliable flight behavior ease of printing and an enjoyable user experience. The result is a lightweight canard aircraft optimized for stable and forgiving glide performance while still preserving the unique aerodynamic character and visual identity of a true experimental canard aircraft. At the same time, one of the biggest goals throughout the project was simply to spread as much joy as possible by creating an aircraft that people of all ages could print, launch, experiment with, and enjoy outdoors together.

description: Sound demonstration This a more musical version of my Mini Bass Tube that can play a few notes. This is a membrane instrument that uses a piece of thin nitrile/latex glove or a balloon to produce sound. It doesn't require skill to produce the sound, just blow into the mouthpiece and it creates pitch. This instrument is not loud and produces a pretty low pitch. Normal configuration has 4 hole and is quite easy to use, but there is also a 5 hole print profile for people who want a bit more notes and can handle a more tricky finger positions. HOW TO ASSEMBLE: Remove supports from the mouthpiece. Poking from the top is easiest way to remove it. Take a thin nitrile/ latex glove or a ballon and very lighlty stretch it over the mouthpiece. Not a lot of tension is needed, you are just trying to remove big wrinkles from the surface. Secure the mebrane with the ring to keep it in place. Put the mouthpiece on top of the body and check the sound. For instrument to play best, pitch with all holes closed should be G or A. If pitch is to high or if it's too hard to blow, then remove the ring and reapply with less stretch/tension. If pitch is too low or it produces more of a rattle then a stable note, then reapply the ring with a little bit more tension. When you are happy with the sound you can trim excess membrane for a cleaner look. If the fit between mouthpiece and body is too loose apply a layer of painters tape to the top as shown in the picture. Alternatively you can use bluetack or just glue parts together. There are 4 and 5 hole versions available. I recommend trying the 4 hole version first. Notes are opened one by one starting with the right hand in the order shown in the diagram below. 0 - all holes closed. 4 Holes - Playing notes 0,1,2,3 will give first four notes of a minor scale. Playing notes 0,2,3,4 will give first four notes of a blues scale. 5 Holes - Playing notes 0,1,2,3,5 will give first five notes of a minor scale. Playing notes 0,2,3,4,5 will give first five notes of a blues scale. Here is the video of all the notes being played on the 5 hole variant to demonstrate how to position the fingers. That's it, now you can have fun with it! If you have any questions ask them in the comments I'll try to help.

Prepare Printed Parts Remove the brim from the pen body and clean the top edge with a deburring tool. This is an upgraded revision of my previously released tool storage box ( Bambu H2D/H2S/P2S Tool Storage Box ). What’s new in this update? Improved latch design: The latches in the previous version could come loose easily. This update optimizes the latch structure by adding a click-in notch to each latch, so you get a satisfying “click” when closing the box, and the latches stay securely closed without loosening. Multiple interchangeable inner trays: To better suit users with multiple printers and spare nozzle sets, I’ve added several new inner tray configurations to choose from. Print only the trays you need for your setup. Taller 1.2cm height option: Based on user requests for more storage space, I’ve added a new version with an increased height of 1.2 cm. Standard Version Dimensions: 18.2*10.58*4.4cm; Tall Version Dimensions: 18.2*10.58*5.6cm. The bottom space is divided into 3 cells for easier storage of small accessories. Optional standalone latch (for replacement if printing fails): While the box is designed to be printed as a single piece (print-in-place), some users experienced latch failures during printing. I’ve included a standalone latch part that you can print separately and install if needed—this way, you don’t have to discard the entire box if the latch fails. (Fingers crossed you won’t need it—hope your print goes perfectly on the first try!) What stayed the same? The base length and width are unchanged. If you printed the old version, your existing inner trays will still fit perfectly in this updated box. Usage Tips Due to printing tolerances, some users may find the latches too tight after printing. You can try pressing them firmly into place—when closing the latches, it is recommended to press the middle section instead of the bottom. The latches will become smooth after a few uses. If they are still too tight, you can gently sand the position shown in the illustration with a file, sanding a small amount each time and trying repeatedly to avoid over-sanding. Key Compatibility Note The nozzle slots in the inner trays are specifically designed for Bambu Lab’s quick-change hotend nozzles. This storage box is compatible with accessories from all Bambu printers that use these quick-release nozzles, including the H2D, H2S, P2S, X2D, A1, and A1 mini.

description: SnapBrush Minimalist Auto-Close Toothbrush Holder A minimalist print-in-place toothbrush holder designed for everyday convenience. That’s also why the ventilation openings were intentionally designed to stay mostly hidden on the back and bottom instead of directly facing outward. After release, several users raised valid concerns regarding hygiene, moisture buildup, and long-term cleanliness for bathroom-related 3D prints. After reading all the feedback, I decided not to ignore the discussion and instead updated the project with 2 additional print profiles featuring a new vent-grid bottom design for improved airflow and drainage. The new vent-grid profiles include: improved bottom airflow additional drainage openings modifier-based breathable mesh bottom structure The mesh area is printed without top/bottom layers to allow moisture to escape more easily and improve ventilation. That said, regular cleaning is still highly recommended like any other bathroom accessory. I really appreciate all the constructive discussion and feedback around this project 🙌 Print-in-Place Design No assembly required . Just remove the supports after printing and it’s ready to use. Designed to fit most standard toothbrushes on the market. (Electric toothbrush compatibility may vary depending on handle size.) Size: 28 × 42 × 47 mm Portable & Detachable Design The wall mount and toothbrush holder are separated into two parts. The wall hook can stay mounted permanently using: double-sided tape or countersunk screws (CSK holes included) When needed, simply lift the entire toothbrush case off the wall and bring it with you for travel. Easy to dock back into place after use. Print Notes Adaptive layer height is recommended for the best surface quality. Compatible with: PLA PETG Most common filaments 0.4 nozzle recommended. Print time is under 2 hours. No brim required. To reduce shrink marks and improve appearance, “Slow Down for Overhangs” is disabled in the print profile. Support Options Profile 1 – Standard Support No AMS required. Bridge flow is tuned to 1.5 and 0.2 mm support top Z distance to improve support surface quality. Support removal may require slightly more force, but this setup gives a much cleaner supported surface compared to standard settings. Profile 2 – Support Material Interface AMS required. Optimized for dedicated support interface materials to achieve an extremely clean support surface. Only one small supported area uses interface material support layer set to 4 layer for better support top finishing, so filament switching happens only 4 times and does not significantly increase print time. description: Ford Sierra Sapphire RS Cosworth Style Wheelie Bin Wheel Covers Give your wheelie bin a proper late 80’s and early 90’s performance upgrade with these Ford Sierra Sapphire RS Cosworth inspired wheel covers. Designed to fit standard UK wheelie bin wheels (125mm), these covers recreate the distinctive alloy wheel styling from the legendary Sierra Sapphire RS Cosworth. Perfect for adding a bit of retro Fast Ford energy to bin day without needing complicated printing setups or multi-colour hardware. No AMS is required. Simply add a pause at layer 6, swap filament, and continue printing with the silver sections beginning at layer 5. The covers mount directly onto the original wheelie bin wheels using Bambu MakerSupply BT2x6 self tapping screws for a clean and secure fit (listed in the Bill of Materials). Before you start Clean your print bed and hot end Clean your plate first, following your usual routine. Dish soap works best, clean and then rinse thoroughly, ensure the plate is dry and free of debris before putting back in the printer. Leftover filament residue on your hot end can cause unwanted colour streaks. Please inspect your hot end before starting the print, if you spot any clumps or leftover filament, follow Bambu's recommended cleaning guide to remove. Hardware required Bambu MakerSupply BT2x6 self tapping screws (linked in the BoM) Wheelie Bin! ----- Printer setup No AMS is required for this print. To achieve the two-colour effect: Print the first six layers in black Add a manual pause at layer 4 in the slicer Swap to silver filament Resume printing from layer 5 onwards ----- Printing Recommended settings The supplied 3MF profile is recommended for the intended fit and appearance, adaptive layer height us used to help with smoother curves / chamfers. Please choose filament suitable for the weather in your area. These test prints are in PLA, but I will be ordering some PLA Tough which I've listed in the Bill of Materials. Layer change The silver sections begin at layer 5. If not using an AMS: Insert a pause at layer 4 Change filament before continuing the print ----- Assembly Fitting the covers Position each cover centrally over the existing wheelie bin wheel and secure using the Bambu MakerSupply BT2x6 self tapping screws. I peronsally drilled a very small starting hole, then used a hex screwdriver (for applying pressure easier) to screw them in place. Do not overtighten the screws, especially when using PLA, as excessive force may crack the print. Outdoor use For long-term outdoor exposure, PLA Tough, PETG or ASA is recommended over standard PLA. ----- Troubleshooting Colours not lining up correctly Make sure the filament change occurs after layer 4. The silver sections start at layer 5. Please test this in your slicer if unsure. ----- Disclaimer This is a fan-made design inspired by the classic Ford Sierra Sapphire RS Cosworth alloy wheel styling. This model let's you make your own custom bookfinity books inside Bambu Studio. Just select a book size, change the text, and upload an image to make your custom book to store your stuff. What is Bookfinity? Bookfinity is a storage system that let's you store gridfinity stuff inside custom book shelf toolboxes. These look fantastic on a bookshelf and let's you grab your tools and components with ease. It's the most organised storage solution for any hobby. It consists of two parts: a bottom part which holds the part, and a top cover that includes the hinge. These two parts are aligned with the tabs and need superglue to attach together (Assembly Instructions below). Update (18-05-2026) I've re-exported every book size to have wider tolerances on the hinge, this should make it easier for those struggling with hinge issues. Thanks for your patience with this fix. How to use this Easy Edit Model? Step 1 - Select your book thickness Find the book size you want to edit. The 3MF files are organized by the bin height, eg 3U Books take 3U bins. Each profile has the following sizes: 2x2, 2x3, 3x3, 3x4, 3x5, 4x4. Step 2 - Select your book Select your book size, and rotate the screen so you're looking underneath like this: Step 3 - Change to Objects On the left hand side, change the Process from Global to Objects. Step 4 - Click on your book Click on the book on the build bed, you'll see the text options on the left hand side. Step 5 - Select Edit Text Right click the main text and press “Edit Text”. A popup will appear Step 6 - Change the text Change the input text and you can change the size and move it around. (You can change the font too, but certain fonts don't print too well). Step 7a - Create an SVG (optional) There are many free SVGs online, and I've uploaded all of the SVGs I've used on Bookfinity on this model. If you need a custom one, you can use ChatGPT with the following prompt: “Create an image of an svg-style stencil with thick black lines of: ” and insert the name of the tool. Step 7b - Convert the PNG to SVG (optional) If you create a PNG, you'll need to convert it to an SVG. You can do it with a free site like FreeConvert. Step 8 - Insert the SVG Right click your book, press “Add Modifier” > “SVG”. TIP: if you insert your SVG, and it's just a rectangle this is because the SVG has an outline / border. This is wrong and won't work. If you generated the SVG using FreeConvert or similar, try change one of the options. on FreeConvert, I found if you go to Advanced Settings and change the "Color Mode" to “Black & White” and redownload it, it fixes this issue. Step 9 - Move, Scale and Rotate your SVG Using the Move, Scale and Rotate buttons, get your SVG where you need it. Step 10 - Set the depth of the SVG Firstly find your SVG on the menu on the left (remember to press “Objects” if you've gone off it). Right click it and press “Edit SVG”. A popup will appear. On the popup, set the Depth to 0.60mm and ensure the “From Surface” distance is 0.00mm. You can use “Use Surface” but it makes it invisible on the prepare tab so harder to use. Step 11 - Set the colour of your SVG On the left hand side, right click the SVG, press “Change Filament” and select the colour you wish to use, eg Black. Step 12: Enable Prime Tower Change Process back to "Global", then under the “Others” tab, find “Prime Tower” and select “Enable”. Move the prime tower so it doesn't clash with your model. This will make the books print much cleaner. Step 13 - Boost the model How to assemble a book Add superglue to the glue area shown below 2. Print a Gridfinity holder for your tool / stuff. description: DESIGN CONCEPT This joint was designed to create a modular frame system composed of vertical and horizontal rods positioned on staggered planes . The main idea behind the project is to use the rods themselves as direct supports for the shelves , allowing the panels to rest inside the structure rather than being mechanically fixed on top of it. This approach creates a lighter and more open construction while maintaining structural stability. The geometry of the joint is inspired by traditional self-built wooden structures , where natural elements such as ropes and vines are used to connect intersecting rods . The overlapping volumes and exposed connections recall this construction principle, giving the system a handcrafted yet contemporary appearance. This solution makes it possible to create a fully self-supporting structure composed exclusively of rods and joints , increasing flexibility in the overall configuration and allowing different shelving layouts to be assembled with a minimal number of components . The Staggered Joint does not include multiple structural variants. Instead, the system uses a mirrored version of the same joint , allowing symmetrical assembly throughout the shelving structure while maintaining visual consistency. The geometry has been carefully optimized for FDM 3D printing , ensuring: Good mechanical performance (max load per shelf: 7Kg, with a shelving unit of maximum 5 shelves ) Stable connection between staggered rods Easy and intuitive assembly In the image below, you can see the joint integrated into the shelving structure. These dimensions follow the most common semi-finished wood sizes in the European market . SPECS & FEATURES This joint is designed to build a modular shelving system using: 30 × 30 mm square wooden rods* 18-30 mm thick wooden panels* *(originally based on European wood semi-finished standard measures) The system allows you to create custom shelving structures (maximum 5 shelves) with a minimal number of parts, with a max load per shelf of 7Kg TIPS & TRICKS For maximum strength and durability: Secure the joints to the panels using wood screws into the dedicated holes (not mandatory, the structure works anyway)* Print with 100% infill Based on structural analysis, we recommend not exceeding 800 mm plank length *The joint tolerances have been optimized for a standard wood thickness commonly available on the European market, ensuring strong and stable connections. Screws were introduced as an additional precaution because commercially available wood panels can sometimes present slight dimensional variations (for example, 2.8–2.9 mm instead of the nominal 3.0 mm). These small discrepancies may reduce the effectiveness of the rod connection, whose tolerances were calibrated during the design process, leading to the need of screws. We would love to see your shelves! If you print this project, share photos of your build and let others see how you used the system. Happy printing! description: SafeMount ist eine modulare Wandhalterung mit Sicherheitsmechanismus, die auf maximale Belastbarkeit bei minimalem Materialeinsatz ( < 13g ) optimiert wurde. Die Halterung besteht aus einer robusten Wandbasis, einem Gleitschienen-Gegenstück und einem Sicherungsbolzen für eine zuverlässige Verriegelung. Konstruktive Merkmale Die mechanischen Eigenschaften von SafeMount basieren auf einer konischen V-Führung (Schwalbenschwanz-Prinzip) . Diese Geometrie bietet entscheidende Vorteile: Selbstzentrierung: Der Clip wird beim Einhängen intuitiv in die Endposition geführt (Guided Entry). Spielfreier Sitz: Unter Last verkeilt sich das System selbstständig, was jegliches mechanisches Spiel eliminiert. Intelligenter Sicherungsmechanismus Das Highlight von SafeMount ist der integrierte Sicherheitsverschluss: Vorbereitung: Der Sicherungsbolzen wird vorab in die Schiene (Object Mount) eingesetzt, welche Ihr am Objekt verschraubt, dass Ihr aufhängen wollt. Montage: Das Objekt wird in die montierte Wandbasis (Wall Mount) eingehängt. Verriegelung: Mit einem Schraubendreher wird der Sicherungsbolzen nun in Basis gedrückt. Dadurch ist ein unbeabsichtigtes Ausheben (etwa durch Stöße von unten) physikalisch ausgeschlossen. Die Verbindung ist formschlüssig gesichert und lässt sich nur gezielt wieder lösen. Druck- & Materialeigenschaften Das Design ist konsequent für eine horizontale Druckausrichtung und eine Layerhöhe von 0,16 mm optimiert. Dadurch wirkt die Last als Scherspannung quer zu den Layern, was die Belastbarkeit im Vergleich zum stehenden Druck massiv steigert. Die Bohrungen sind mit 4,2 mm angelegt, um nach dem materialbedingten Schrumpf eine ideale Passung für Standard-Schrauben (ca. 4 mm) zu gewährleisten. 13.05.2026 - Revision 1 Nach Nutzerfeedback und einigen weiteren Tests haben wir in Revision 1 die Wandbasis optimiert, da wir genau wie ihr ein absolut verlässliches System wollen. Die wichtigste Neuerung ist die Gewährleistung einer deutlich besseren Kraftverteilung durch eine nun durchgehende Wandstärke von 4,75 mm statt der bisherigen 1,78 mm an den Flanken. Da wir die Wanddicke vereinheitlicht haben, werden Spannungsspitzen eliminiert und die Last wird besser abgeleitet. Die Verstärkung des Materials an den Führungsschienen verhindert zudem das Aufbiegen der Basis unter Hebelwirkung, was die Sicherheit im Vergleich zur Initialversion erheblich steigert. Hier noch der Vergleich zur ersten Variante im Querschnitt: Belastungswerte & Challenge In statischen Tests wurden Lasten von 10 kg ohne strukturelles Versagen nachgewiesen. Für den täglichen Einsatz empfehlen wir eine Last von bis zu 5 kg . Bei Verwendung als Regalhalterung (Hebelwirkung) empfehlen wir die Nutzung von mindestens zwei Haltern und eine Reduzierung der maximalen Traglast je nach Hebeltiefe - leichte Regale für dekorative Elemente. Da wir in der Werkstatt zwar gute Ideen, aber kein professionelles Zugkraftmessgerät haben, brauchen wir euch: Wer hat Lust, SafeMount kontrolliert an die Belastungsgrenze zu treiben? Schickt uns eure Bilder oder Daten vom Bruchtest. Den ersten „Master of Destruction“ mit validen Messwerten verewigen wir namentlich mit seinen Daten hier in der Beschreibung!

description: Lucky Knot Maker | Easy Chinese Knot Tool The 「Pan Long Knot」 symbolizes “endless life, lasting happiness, and peace” — a classic emblem of traditional Chinese lucky culture. This is a tool to help you weave a Pan Long Knot (a type of Chinese knot). I made it because I loved doing knot crafts as a kid. In middle school, our handicraft class started a knotting unit — and I ended up doing the homework for half the class. I became a hero. Those are really fond memories. I once designed a 3D printed Chinese knot that used hinges to mimic the soft texture of the real one. Chinese Knot · Pan Long Knot - Free 3D Print Model - MakerWorld Now, I wanted to go a step further — create a tool that makes the weaving process itself easy and enjoyable for everyone. The model is a base plate printed with the weaving pattern, featuring guide rails and clips to hold the cord securely. (Traditional methods use pins on foam — messy, a bit risky, and sometimes damage the cord.) I also included a picking tool that stores in a slot on the plate — it helps lift the cord when you need to pass under it. (Inspired by the NDS stylus 😄) For detailed steps, please read the Assembly guide . Once you understand the method, you can complete the knot just by following the hints on the model. You’ll need a cord of at least 2.4m long, about 2mm in diameter — red works best. Printing tip: The base plate fits on the A1 mini, but you need to disable the prime tower. Once all parts are printed, secure them with glue. Multi-color printing makes the weaving guide lines on the base plate more visible. If you don't have AMS, printing in a single color works just fine — the tool remains fully functional. About the contest: I didn’t create this model specifically for it, but after finishing, I realized it fits the theme quite well: it carries a lucky meaning, offers a fun and accessible hands‑on process, and is perfectly safe. description: What It Is Anyone who works regularly with small neodymium magnets knows the problem. You organize them carefully, and at some point they have already found their way into a cluster; stuck to every ferromagnetic screw sharing the same drawer, bridging across compartments, and occasionally jamming the whole thing shut. The drawer refuses to open because a group of magnets has settled into just the right alignment to block it. This product came directly from that frustration. The Magnet Storage is a 3D-printable dispenser designed to keep magnets contained, separated, and accessible, one at a time, without the usual mayhem. Difficulty level: beginner . Assembly only requires a screwdriver. MagSet - Magnet Insertion Tool The companion tool for the Magnet Storage is already available. The MagSet - Magnet Insertion Tool , I will be adding more and more sizes in the comming days Key Features Dispenser-style access: magnets are retrieved individually, which keeps the rest of the batch undisturbed - Up to 80 magnets per storage unit Easy to detach magnets from the stack Prevents spontaneous clustering during storage Designed to minimize contact with surrounding ferromagnetic materials Compatible with multiple magnet diameters (see available profiles) Assembled with self-tapping screws only Compact enough to sit on a workbench or integrate into a larger storage setup Hardware Materials and assembly 5x BT2.6x8 SHCS Self-Tapping screws - For magnets of 6 mm diameter or more 5x BT2x5 SHCS Self-Tapping screws - For magnets of 5 mm diameter or less Note: The magnet with a diameter of 3mm (CA014) and lower (CA014) is very small, so this is a special case The usual BT2x5 SHCS Self-Tapping screws are large. In this case, you should insert the magnets without the bolts on the bottom, but the first one should have a small drop of cyanoacrylate glue to permanently secure it to the container. You still need: 1x BT2x5 SHCS Self-Tapping screws - for the top cap In principle, any ferromagnetic screw of the appropriate size will work mechanically. That said, ferromagnetic fasteners placed near magnets will attract them, which can complicate assembly. The self-tapping screws listed above are the tested choice and the recommended starting point. Assembly sequence Magnets Buying the magnets through the links below is a practical way to support the project if you found it useful: See Bill of materials Print Materials No special filament required. Standard PLA works for most use cases. PETG is worth considering if the dispenser will be more durable. Anyway, just do't use TPU ;) Design Notes The usual approach to magnet storage is a divided tray or compartmentalized drawer. It seems logical, but magnets are persistent: given enough of them in proximity, they will bridge compartments, attract nearby hardware, and generally resist the idea of staying put. A jammed drawer is the mild version of the problem. The approach here is different. Rather than trying to contain chaos inside a closed space, the dispenser controls how magnets are accessed. The stored batch stays undisturbed while you interact with one magnet at a time. It is a small shift in logic, but it makes daily use noticeably less frustrating. Twist the cap or make a lateral movement to remove the number of magnets needed. Future Plans The initial release covers the most common magnet diameters used in maker and 3D printing workflows. Depending on community feedback, versions for larger disc magnets or rod magnets may follow. If a specific size or configuration is missing from your setup, feel free to reach out here or at designrepcom.com .

What It Is Inserting small neodymium magnets into 3D-printed holes is one of those tasks that looks simple until you actually do it. The magnets attract to each other, to nearby tools, and to anything ferromagnetic in reach. Getting them seated cleanly and at the right depth, without disturbing the ones already placed, takes more patience than it should, and when it involves glue, this is taken to another new level of "stikiness". MagSet is a 3D-printable insertion tool designed to make that process faster and more reliable. It is an updated and expanded version of the Magnet Insertion Fast Tool published earlier and addresses the main friction points reported by the community since that release. Difficulty level: beginner . No special skills required. New Version Earlier version What Changed From the Previous Version The original tool worked well for most users, but a recurring complaint was that the part could occasionally detach from the build plate during printing. A more thorough build plate cleaning likely would have solved it in most cases, but the redesign eliminates the issue by significantly increasing the contact area with the build plate. The tool will stay put. Beyond that, two things drove the new design. Ergonomics were improved to make repeated use more comfortable, and the tool is now available in sizes that cover all magnet diameters sold by Bambu Lab, which the previous version did not fully address. How It Works The tool uses a piston mechanism. The magnet attaches to the tip of the piston — held in place by a ferromagnetic screw or by a bonded reference magnet, depending on the variant — and is then pressed into the target hole with controlled, light force applied through the palm. The contact surface at the top is shaped to distribute that force naturally and to discourage applying more load than the tool is designed for. That is a deliberate choice, not a limitation. Key Features Larger build plate footprint compared to the previous version: no detachment during printing Ergonomic grip geometry that limits applied force by design, protecting both the tool and the printed part Covers all neodymium magnet diameters available from Bambu Lab Three assembly variants to suit different magnet sizes and available hardware Hollow shaft section on the piston, increasing the local moment of inertia and improving mechanical performance without adding material Compatible with the Magnet Storage system as part of a complete magnet management workflow Magnet Storage Materials Print material Any rigid filament works. PLA is the default and performs well for this application. PETG, ABS, or ASA are all acceptable alternatives. TPU should not be used — the tool requires stiffness to function correctly. Assembly — three options depending on magnet size: Option 1 — Self-tapping screw: A single ferromagnetic SHCS self-tapping screw holds the magnet to the piston tip magnetically. Two sizes are supported: BT2x8 (AA004) BT2.6x8 (AA019) The screw does not clamp anything mechanically; its only function is to provide a ferromagnetic surface that attracts and holds the magnet in position. Any ferromagnetic screw of equivalent size will work. Option 2 — No hardware (PLA only) - Bonded reference magnet (cyanoacrylate). For magnets 3mm diameter and smaller, a same-diameter magnet is glued to the piston tip with cyanoacrylate adhesive. This bonded magnet then attracts and holds the working magnets during insertion. Required only for the smallest diameter variants. An exploded view shows the assembly with the self-tapping bolt A Note on Loads The piston shaft includes a hollow section designed to improve its moment of inertia, which helps mechanical performance. That said, plastic is plastic, and FDM printed parts are anisotropic — meaning their strength varies depending on the direction of the applied force, which is a fundamental characteristic of layer-by-layer manufacturing. This tool is designed for light insertion loads, which is also why the top surface is shaped the way it is: for use with your palm. If your application requires pressing magnets in with significant force, that points to a different tool category altogether. If there is enough interest in a high-force variant, that is something that could be developed separately. Magnets Buying the magnets through the links below is a practical way to support the project if you found it useful: See Bill of materials The Magnet Storage system, also available on MakerWorld, keeps all those magnet sizes organized and ready to use alongside this tool. Design Notes The design follows the same visual language as recent projects: clean lines, no excess material, functional geometry that does not hide what it is doing. The hollow piston shaft is the one element that rewards a closer look — it is there for a structural reason, not for aesthetics, though the two are not mutually exclusive. Hallow spaces on the piston shaft And some some theory on material mechanics If you look at the piston shaft closely, you will notice it is not solid. There is a hollow section along its length, and that is not there to save material or print time. It is a structural decision. When a slender part bends under load , the material at the very center of the cross-section contributes almost nothing to resisting that bending. The fibers that actually do the work are the ones furthest from the neutral axis, at the outer edges (in this case, buckling may accur) . This is the principle behind the second moment of area, sometimes called the moment of inertia in structural terms: moving material away from the center and toward the periphery increases a section's resistance to bending without necessarily adding more material overall. It is the same reason steel I-beams are shaped the way they are. By making the shaft hollow rather than solid, the outer wall carries the load more efficiently. The result is a piston that handles the bending forces involved in magnet insertion better than a solid rod of the same diameter would. That said, FDM printed parts are anisotropic , meaning their mechanical properties are not the same in every direction. Strength along the print layers is considerably higher than strength across them, which is a fundamental characteristic of the process and not something geometry alone can fully compensate for. The hollow shaft helps, but it does not change the nature of the material. Keep the loads light, and the tool will serve you well for a long time.

model_name: Any Size HexGrid Pen Holder - SIMPLE CUSTOMIZATION
description: A modular, space-efficient organizer for alcohol markers — fully customizable! Note - this is a simplified version of my Any Size Honeycomb Marker Pen Holder (Ohuhu/Copic) model, with only the most important subset of the customization options to make it more intuitive to use. If you want more customization options, feel free to visit it! A hexagonal (honeycomb) pen holder optimized for alcohol markers like Ohuhu, Copic, and similar dual-tip markers. The angled, elongated hexagonal cells make insertion and removal effortless while maximizing space efficiency. The size is customizable — make as large a grid as you need! The included print profile has a 8x11 version with base and a 4x11 version without - you can glue both together to make a large, 132-holder version. And you're not limited to that - you can create your own thanks to the Customizer! 4x11 without base 8x11 with base Both glued together: 12x11 KEY FEATURES Angled design for easy access — the 25º default tilt (adjustable) combined with extra cell height makes inserting and removing markers smooth and intuitive. The taller cells provide a larger "target area" so you can easily grab the marker you want, and neighboring markers can shift aside naturally when you reach in. Can be used vertically or horizontally, with two variants provided for different needs: Vertical base (default) — with extended length to keep the holder stable even when full No base — for use in the horizontal direction for lightweight pens, or for stacking vertically on top of another holder Space-efficient hexagonal grid — the honeycomb pattern uses space as efficiently as a square grid while being much more ergonomic thanks to staggered rows. The design is also structurally strong and lightweight. Models with the same parameters fit together well horizontally. Parametric — change grid dimensions (rows × columns) and angle in the included .scad file or directly in the Customizer . NOTE : The full model has more parameters - for example, you can change the cell size to hold other types of pen, tools, etc. WHAT'S INCLUDED 8x11 model with vertical base + 4x11 freestanding model in two plates — print just the first plate for a large 8x11 standalone, or print and glue both together for a huge, 12x11, 132 marker holder OpenSCAD source file (.scad) — customize any parameter to create grids from 1×1 to 10×10+ (or asymmetric sizes), change the angle, select base type, etc. Note regarding .scad file availability : Unfortunately, due to plagiarism from other users, I have hidden the SCAD source code for the time being. You can use the Customizer, or just contact me - I'll be happy to provide it for any legitimate use you might have (including just wanting to look at it). DIMENSIONS FOR THE PROVIDED MODELS 8x11 12x11 (two pieces) Markers held 88 132 Approximate footprint (WxDxH, cm) 20.5 × 12.2 × 22 20.5 × 12.2 × 26 Tilt angle ( alpha ) 25º This lovely setup uses 3 12x11 holders (provided profile - print 3 8x11, 3 4x11 standalone, and glue each pair together to get a 12x11 holder), plus an extra 6x10 holder (left, comes from a previous iteration of the model). The 3 large holders fit 396 pens - almost enough for the full 320-set plus a 80-set. CUSTOMIZATION GUIDE Open the attached .scad file in OpenSCAD or in the MakerWorld customizer and adjust the parameters as follows. wx — number of cells horizontally (default 11) wy — number of cells vertically (default 11 for regular / 4 for freestanding) alpha — inclination angle in degrees (default 25º; decrease for easier access, increase for more compact footprint). withBase — choose whether to add a base or not. You can make larger holders by gluing together models with and without base. The model is particularly well suited to narrow spaces, for which holders are hard to come by. This is the 6x10 holder from a previous iteration of the model, originally sized to fit into a specific nook. A note on vertical stacking Print a model with withBase = false and glue or snap it on top of a standard one with a vertical base to extend your storage vertically without reprinting the base. Great for expanding a collection incrementally. IMPORTANT NOTE: if you intend to extend the model vertically by gluing together several pieces, it's best if the number of rows is even. Horizontal use You can also use the model horizontally, so that it lies down on the table instead of vertically. Great for brushes or if your vertical space is restricted. You might want to set withBase = false as the base won't be needed, and use a shallow alpha (0º to 15º) to increase stability. Side-by-side pairing Models fit pretty well together horizontally - they will not be flush because of the honeycomb geometry, but the separation between the vertical walls is small. You can glue the slanted walls of the honeycomb together: Models fit together with a small horizontal separation, but with ample contact surface for glue if needed (all the slanted lateral walls). You can do cool things by gluing together narrow holders: A simulation of a rainbow holder composed of 6 2x10 individual holders. PRINTING RECOMMENDATIONS Material: PLA or PETG Supports: None needed. The standard values (15% grid, 2 walls) work fine for most cases. The default wall size (0.8mm) works well for a standard 0.4mm nozzle. If you want thicker or thinner walls, you can customize the width in the full model. WHY HEXAGONS? Square grids waste space in the gaps between round pens. Hexagonal packing is mathematically optimal — you get similar spacing between pen centers but with better accessibility because of the staggered rows. The honeycomb structure is also incredibly strong for its weight. Plus, it looks cool. TESTED COMPATIBILITY This holder is designed for dual-tip alcohol markers with bodies around 16-16.5mm in diameter, including: Ohuhu markers Copic Sketch/Ciao Touchnew Shuttle Art Spectrum Noir Most other alcohol-based dual-tip markers For other pen types (or objects), you can use the customizer in the full model to change the grid size accordingly.

SCROCKET - The Screaming Rocket! Throw it, hear it, love it! Spring time is outdoor time! Take my latest creation with you to the park! We all remember these rockets that screached when being thrown. I decided to attempt at creating one myself. I designed this throwing rocket which is to be printed in multiple parts. It has some clip in whistles that can be interchanged for different tunes. The model has a variety of infills to optimize the center of gravity for optimal flight properties. For printing I used Shore 95 A TPU. If you want to print it with an AMS you need to use Bambus TPU for AMS Shore 68D, which is similar in properties. It is planned to release new, improved and different sounding whistles in the near future. I hope you enjoy playing with it. Disclaimer: This is kind of a work in progress. I might be changing the geometry and modifiers in the print profile to optimize aerodynamics. Assembly: The parts are designed to have a very snug and tight fit so you don't need to reassemble it everytime it crashlanded somewhere. That means you will need some small pliers to assemble. I assembled it this way (Please ignore the dirt on the model, it has been to the park with me already): Threaded parts First I screwed in the threaded parts, compressing the parts with outer threads just at the upper thread and and screwing it in. I found it the easiest way to do this. Fins Then I slid in the fins from the back and pulled them forward using a small pair of pliers. The tail bit itsself will flex when you pull it along like this, but you can just hold the fin in place with your pliers and gently bend back the tail. Wiggle each fin in like this. Whistles For the whistles i pushed the parts in on one side and then used a small nail file to get underneath the lip and push them in with some leverage. I had to go around the hole for a tiny bit, just like mounting a bike tire! Please feel free to contact me whenever you have feedback, requests or questions on the model!

This model is a thank you to everyone who made this possible. The Lockheed U-2 , known as the Dragon Lady , is one of the most iconic high-altitude reconnaissance aircraft ever built. Designed during the Cold War, it operates at extreme altitudes of 70,000+ feet , where the sky fades into the darkness of space and the curvature of the Earth becomes visible. Fun facts: The U-2 flies so high that pilots must wear full pressure suits , similar to astronauts. At its operating altitude, the difference between stall speed and maximum speed is only a few knots, known as the “coffin corner.” It has such long wings that it behaves more like a glider than a typical jet aircraft. Landing requires a chase car on the runway to guide the pilot, because visibility and depth perception are extremely limited. This MasterBuilds model captures the unique proportions of the U-2 with its long wings and slender fuselage, while keeping the signature snap-fit assembly and efficient print design. Oversized Opening: The entry hole and internal cavity are designed to be more than big enough for standard squirrels. Quick & Easy Exit: The interior is spacious and restriction-free, so if a squirrel gets startled, they can back out instantly and make a quick getaway without getting stuck. description: Key Features This design focuses on improved drying performance and reliable printing. The dual unit construction spreads silica gel out into two containers, allowing for better silica gel regeneration within a filament dryer. The fully meshed walls allows for all 6 sides to be fully exposed to air for better efficacy. The woven structure of the mesh walls ensures reliable printing with minimal small start-stop print retractions, minimising the risk of excessive stringing or potential clogging with some filaments. Optimised high surface area mesh for reliable printing and greater exposed surface area for all 6 sides Dual unit design for easy removal within the AMS without removing spools ~350g dry silica gel capacity (20-30% heavier for wet silica gel) Compatible with AMS 2 Pro and AMS (the original AMS will have a looser fit) 1.1mm diameter hole size suitable for desiccant beads >1.5mm Designed for silica gel regeneration in mind when printed with a temperature resistant filament Secure latching lid to ensure the lid won't become loose from thermal expansion Print Guidance Please print using the uploaded 3MF print profiles. Do not change the print settings or download the STLs to print from, as there will be no mesh. The mesh is generated using slicer modifiers and settings, so it won't be visible in the 3D model. Please ensure build plate is clean prior to printing. An unclean build plate will cause poor adhesion which will result in issues with the mesh being printed and may also result in prints lifting. Please clean the bed thoroughly with soap and water if having issues. Build plate glue may be required for some challenging filaments. PETG, ABS, ASA filaments are recommend. PLA is not recommended due to low temperature resistance and is somewhat of a stiffer material. Fiber reinforced engineering filaments can be used but the stiffness of material will cause the latch to be quite firm . Please check below for filament specific guidance. Printing with 0.4mm nozzle is recommended for the design. Nozzles with a 0.6mm or 0.8mm diameter will have issues. Filament Type Print Guidance Below are filaments that the design had been test printed with using a 0.4mm nozzle on an X1C. Other filaments may also work. All filaments are recommended to be dried before printing. Bed adhesion can vary depending on filament type and brand, and what build plate is used. Liquid glue stick was used for PC and nylons. description: Diese modulare Rankhilfe ist die perfekte Lösung für Tomaten, Paprika und alle Kletterpflanzen im Garten oder Gewächshaus. Das System kombiniert 3D-Druck mit der Stabilität von Standard-Elektroinstallationsrohren (EN16) :) Warum dieses System? Vollständig Modular: Deine Pflanze wächst? Kein Problem! Füge einfach weitere Etagen hinzu, während die Pflanze größer wird. Kosteneffizient: Statt teure Komplettsysteme zu kaufen, nutzt du günstiges EN16-Rohr aus dem Baumarkt, das du individuell auf deine Wunschhöhe zuschneiden kannst. Die Druckteile sind Leicht Modelliert jedoch durch die Form sehr stabil. Geringerer Filamentverbrauch und schnell gedruckt. Einfacher Druck & Aufbau: Der Ring besteht aus drei identischen Segmenten, die werkzeuglos zusammengesteckt werden. Stabil & Sicher: Die gedruckten Erdspieße sorgen für festen Halt im Boden, während die Ringe Äste und Früchte sicher stützen. Technische Details: Rohrdurchmesser: Optimiert für Standard EN16 Isolierrohr (starr). !!! Für Alle die keine Möglichkeit oder Lust haben an ein EN16 Rohr zu kommen, wurden Rohre zum Drucken hinzugefügt. Diese Können in Z achse im Slicer auf gewünschte länge skaliert werden!!! Ring-Design: 3-Teiler-Stecksystem (kein Kleber nötig). Druck: Getestet in PETG (empfohlen für Außenanwendungen/Gewächshaus wegen UV- und Hitzebeständigkeit). 1. Drucken: Drucke pro Etage drei Ring-Segmente. Für die Basis benötigst du zusätzlich die entsprechenden 3 Erdspieße. Empfehlung: Nutze PETG oder ASA für eine lange Lebensdauer in der Sonne. 2. Rohre vorbereiten: Besorge dir EN16 Elektroinstallationsrohre im Baumarkt. Schneide diese mit einer Säge auf die gewünschte Höhe zu. Du kannst die Rohre jederzeit gegen längere austauschen oder mit Muffen verlängern. 3. Montage der Ringe: Stecke jeweils drei identische Ring-Segmente ineinander, bis sie einen geschlossenen Kreis bilden. 4. Stecke die zugesägte EN16 Rohre von unten in die Ringteile (Je nach ausfürhung könnten diese etwas streng reingehen. Falls nötig mit schleifpapier die Rohre nacharbeiten) 5. Erdspieße auf die rohre draufstecken und ab in die erde damit. 6. Falls notwendig noch eine etage zusammenbauen und ohne erdspieße auf die untere etage setzen. Wenn die Pflanze wächst, kannst du neue Ringe einfach von oben hinzufügen, ohne die Pflanze zu beschädigen.
