description: Join Breeze Model Pilot Group here https://www.facebook.com/groups/1165452208203912 ---------------------------- Intro The Breeze Model X is the latest addition to the "Breeze" series of RC planes. Customizable upgrades Lightweight yet strong Modular design SUB250 compliant Few parts to assemble Completely FREE to download License: Breeze Model X is available for free download and non-commercial use only when downloaded exclusively from MakerWorld.com . Please contact me for authorization if you wish to use it beyond the Standard Digital File License. As I will continuously enhance this model base on your feedback, please revisit here for updates. The Breeze Model X is a SUB250 modular flying wing, designed to weigh less than 250g, allowing for easy compliance with aviation regulations in many countries. This design means you can enjoy flying in most regions without the need for a remote identification tag. However, it's important to verify your local laws and ensure you fly in safe, unpopulated areas since it can go very fast. It flys notable responsiveness, offering a firm yet reactive feel, which suits aerobatic maneuvers. It can rolls and loops easily. Additionally, it features an efficient wingfoil, achieving a tested glide ratio close to 12 (which means it descends 1 meter for every 12 meters it glides). Flying characteristics: In my fly test. Wing Span: 560mm (incl. winglets) RTF weight: ~250g Battery: 3S 1300mAh Motor: 1406 3300kv Prop: Gemfan 3inch 3052 (high pitch blades for speed) Glide Ratio: ~12:1 @ 12m/s Stall speed: 7.5m/s or 27km/h Cruise Speed: 15m/s or 54km/h Top speed : 30m/s or 108km/h Cruise throttle: 50% Cruise Time: 45min Thurst to weight ratio: 0.9 Print Time : ~10 Hours vase mode PLA-Aero or LW-PLA -- Note : Per user feedbacks, if you want to print with non-foaming materials such as PETG, you will need a 3S 18650 pack to get the COG right (normal lipo is too thick for the fuselage and the canopy wont fit). Prepare for heavier wing-load (stall speed will be increased massively) This extended nose parts allows you to fit smaller battery while still making COG right. Thanks to the author https://makerworld.com/en/models/465958#profileId-374847 BOM besides printable parts and Fly Controller 5 x 300mm Carbon Tube x 1 EMAX 9g servo x 2 Push rod 1mm to 1.2mm diameter, at least 11cm length x 2 M3 5mm Nylon screw x 3 (Optional) M3 thread insert x 3 (Optional) Recommended Filaments Bambu Lab ASA-Aero : https://us.store.bambulab.com/products/asa-aero Bambu Lab PLA-Aero : https://us.store.bambulab.com/products/pla-aero Tuning before mainden Mixer setting : Pitch 60% Roll 30% – this is critical, because this plane has large control surface, and roll is too sensitive. INAV PID setting (under testing): I am still finding a good PID, will update you here. Mean while, please reduce roll PIDFF rate which the default values are really unstable. Old setting 2024/04/13: pitch rate: 150 deg/sec roll rate: 310 deg/sec Lower all Roll PID by half. Set roll FF to 60. Lower all Pitch PID by 25%. Set pitch FF to 80. ( Important ) Enable advance PID and lower “level strength” to 8 . Current suggestion 2024/05/03: # Mixer: servo mixer smix reset smix 0 1 0 -30 0 -1 smix 1 1 1 -60 0 -1 smix 2 2 0 -30 0 -1 smix 3 2 1 60 0 -1 # PID and rate setting set fw_p_pitch = 10 set fw_i_pitch = 10 set fw_d_pitch = 5 set fw_ff_pitch = 70 set fw_p_roll = 8 set fw_i_roll = 5 set fw_d_roll = 5 set fw_ff_roll = 51 set fw_p_level = 10 set roll_rate = 30 set pitch_rate = 17 # save configuration save Please give suggestion if you have better turning. Once it is stable, I will export the setting cmd, and you could apply it in one go. /*-----------------------------------------*/ Design Principle Alternative source (Chinese via bilibili): 3D printed RC planes often seem stiff and easy to break, getting damaged from small crashes that foam planes usually handle well. To fix this in my design, I focused on two main ideas: Lightweight and Strong – be SUB250 and resistance to small crash. Modular design – easy to swap broken modules and customized options. Also, foaming filaments (like PLA-Aero, ASA-Aero, LW-PLA, etc.) usually have issues with strings in normal printing. But, a special printing way called spiral vase mode can solve this by drawing the shape's outline all at once without stopping. This needs a special design trick to make sure every layer can be drawn in one go, with each layer sitting right on top of the last one. This lets Bambu Studio make a continuous printing line, avoiding any stops and moves. The design was tricky, but don’t worry about it. I did the hard work, and you can just print with the profiles I shared. NOTE: DO NOT rearrange the foaming parts, they need to be print one each plate with set spiral-vase mode. This flying wing has only 6 parts (3 big and 3 small), which have to be printed one by one in vase mode with foaming filaments. The other parts can be printed all together on one plate with regular filament. There are way fewer foaming parts than other RC planes you might see for sale. And printing this whole plane takes only about 10 hours, which is a lot less time than others that take 50+ hours. Lightweight and strong You might see some red parts in the pictures. Most of these aren't made from foaming material; they're actually for making the plane stronger. While the foaming parts cover a lot of the area and add to the weight, these regular material parts make it much tougher in important spots like where the motor is, the front edge of the wing, the nose, the bottom, and parts that let you swap things easily. These red parts help the wing handle normal landings and minor crashes without getting damaged. The weight ratio between foaming material and regular material is about 4:1. Modular and easy to assembly Even with its lightweight and strong design, the plane can still crash badly. When a crash happens, a typical 3D-printed plane has little chance to survive. But with this design, wings or broken parts can be easily swapped out thanks to the quick-swap connectors, a feature from the start. One of my goals was to make repairs possible right at the flying site. The solution? Make everything changeable. Yes, even wings of this small size have a quick-release system that allows for disassembly in no time, all without a single screw. I always have a set of wings and a body ready to replace any broken parts. During my flight controller tuning and plane optimization, I used up one plane on average each time. However, this wing design does a great job protecting the electronics; I've never lost a servo or any electronic part. The assembly of each module is as simple and straightforward as possible. I really enjoy the building process, and I think you will too. Assembling a complete plane takes less than 30 minutes once you're familiar with it. And you shouldn't need to tune your new plane much, because 3D-printed RC planes always have accurate dimensions. /*-----------------------------------------*/ Assembly Guide Check out the amazing assembly video by McLogo76 Video Assembly Guide video: To be uploaded /*-----------------------------------------*/ Customized your planes I've designed many options to enhance the capabilities of these small wings. Some are aimed at improving flying characteristics, while others boost functionality, like FPV (First-Person View) capabilities. Please see below for the different options available. Winglet options The Lite version, as the default option, is small and lighter, designed to meet the SUB250g regulations. This makes it perfect for those who want a compact and efficient flyer. On the other hand, the Large version offers more lift and better yaw stability, making it suitable for those who prefer a plane that can handle more varied flying conditions. More info please checkout this amazing explain video: FPV cap options The default is the flat top, you may mount your DIY camera on it. Besides, I've also created 2 options to make your FPV setup easier: A 19-20mm top mount with a camera canopy. Print the camera mount with regular filament and glue it on top. A mounting frame for a special O3 camera module taken from BetaFPV Pavo 20 O3 module, can be purchased from their website. It's the most affordable and lightest O3 frame I've found, and it even includes dampers for stabilization. This setup works great, and I highly recommend it. Motor mount options The default motor mount fits 1304 to 150x motors, which are plenty for this small plane. You can try other motors, but remember, larger motors are heavier. You'll likely need to adjust the canopy to fit larger batteries and keep the center of gravity (COG) correct. By the way, the EDF didn't hit the advertised 200g thrust, only reaching 140g. However, it's still flyable and looks very cool. Sled options The spring-loaded sled is for hard surfaces like rocky roads and off-road terrain. Hard surfaces can easily damage foaming parts, so a spring can effectively absorb the vibration and impact, thus protecting the body. For soft surfaces, like grass fields, a hard sled is sufficient. Nose options If you prefer not to mount the camera on top, you can use the camera nose instead of the standard one. It also accommodates a 20mm camera frame for an FPV camera. However, placing the camera at the very front of the wing is quite risky. /*-----------------------------------------*/ More Vids BetaFPV Pavo 20 O3 modual on Breeze MX test video. FPV vid by McLogo76 and his friends! /*-----------------------------------------*/ Tips Rotate your flight controller by 90degree to save some space for battery. Use fast servos, this is a agile wing. Get the COG right, Don't tilt the ailerons up like you might on other wings. This wingfoil already includes that effect, and the twist-wing design also contributes to pitch stabilization.

description: 关联模型：加勒比海盗-阿兹特克金币 https://makerworld.com.cn/zh/models/1630606-jia-le-bi-hai-dao-a-zi-te-ke-jin-bi#profileId-1786022 是知名电影“加勒比海盗”中的风帆战舰——黑珍珠号，陪伴杰克船长在海洋中纵横冒险。 战舰长度363mm，高度278mm（不含底座），宽度128mm。 整个模型除了绳索之外，都是用3D打印制作，组装简单。既可以使用耗材的本色打印，也可以打印白模后涂色。如果你有ams，那么建议使用黑色（或深灰色）和白色耗材打印风帆。 风帆的形状并不是靠打印成型，而是由风帆上的卡扣与桅杆的配合约束成型的。因此风帆都是平铺在热床上打印，可以获得很高的打印质量和速度，而且保持很薄的厚度，更像真实帆船上的布质材料。 我对帆船并没有很深的研究，因此对于上面的索具不是很了解，也许我的索具布置不是很准确，请有这方面专业知识的朋友提出意见和建议，大家一起来改进。 风帆的卡扣很细小，安装时小心一点，以免弄坏。pla lite耗材的层间结合力不够，不建议使用它打印风帆。 如果您喜欢这个作品，请给我点赞、收藏或关注我，这对我有很大的帮助，谢谢！ 后面有组装说明，也可以下载pdf版的说明书 -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 零部件清单 1. 船身-后半段 2. 船身-前半段 3. 绳索支架（6个） 4. 前桅杆（字母标识F） 5. 后桅杆（字母标识R） 6. 中桅杆（字母标识M） 7. 方向舵 8. 瞭望塔（3个） 9. 船首雕像 10. 前身桅杆 11. 底座 12. 甲板-前 13. 甲板-后 14. 帆-中上（字母标识MT） 15. 帆-后上（字母标识RT） 16. 三角帆 17. 帆-前上（字母标识FT） 18. 火炮（30个）有冗余，以防丢失） 19. 帆-中下（字母标识MB） 20. 帆-前下（字母标识FB） 21. 帆-后下（字母标识RB） 22. 船身连接销钉（3个） ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 组装 1. 拆除船身上的辅助支撑 图中蓝色部分是为了在打印时减少支撑而特意设计的冗余结构，与船身本体并未牢固结合，组装前需要拆除它们。 2. 组装前后船身 使用“船身连接销钉”连接前后船身，接缝处涂胶水辅助固定。 3. 安装下层甲板火炮 用胶水把火炮粘到下层甲板上。两个侧舷共16门火炮 4. 安装上层甲板的前半段 请在甲板的边缘涂胶辅助固定 5. 安装上层甲板的后半段 先把甲板后半段倾斜对准前半段的边缘，再向下压，把甲板的前后两段挤压进船身中 测试一下甲板上的两个舱门是否可以正常开合 6. 安装方向舵 在蓝色标识的孔中涂胶，把方向舵插入其中 7. 安装上层火炮 左右两侧各五门火炮，用胶水粘在上层甲板上 8. 安装绳索支架 每侧各三个，先在船身的槽中涂胶，再插入支架 9. 安装桅杆 在甲板的孔中插入前、中、后三根桅杆，每根桅杆上都有字母标识，请注意分辨，不要插错。 如图红圈处，桅杆上有孔的一面朝向船的前方；桅杆插入的深度如图中蓝圈处所示，一定要插到位 10. 安装前伸桅杆 插入的深度如上图所示 11. 安装风帆 每一面风帆都是平整的薄片，需要依靠风帆上的卡扣插入桅杆中，制造出被风鼓起的弯曲效果，风帆的安装位置请参考上图。请在桅杆的孔中涂胶辅助固定风帆。三角帆需要在安装好绳索后再安装。 12. 安装绳索 我对帆船并没有很深的研究，因此对于上面的索具不是很了解，也许我的索具布置不是很准确，请有这方面专业知识的朋友提出意见和建议，大家一起来改进。 13. 安装瞭望塔 14. 安装船首雕像 15. 把黑珍珠号放置在底座上，完成了！

Educational Background: Understanding Earth's internal structure is fundamental in geology, geophysics, and environmental sciences. This model provides an interactive way to explore the composition and function of Earth's layers. Crust: The Earth's outermost layer, composed of solid rock, includes the continental and oceanic crust. It is where all life exists and where tectonic activity, such as earthquakes and volcanic eruptions, occurs. Mantle: Beneath the crust, the mantle makes up about 84% of Earth's volume. It consists of semi-solid rock that moves slowly, driving plate tectonics and causing geological phenomena like mountain formation and continental drift. Outer Core: Composed mainly of liquid iron and nickel, the outer core plays a crucial role in generating Earth's magnetic field through the process of convection. Inner Core: The Earth's innermost layer is a solid sphere made of iron and nickel. Despite its extreme temperatures, immense pressure keeps it in a solid state. The inner core contributes to the stabilization of the planet's magnetic field, which protects Earth from solar radiation. This model offers a hands-on way to visualize these layers, making it an excellent tool for teachers, students, and anyone interested in Earth sciences. By allowing users to detach and examine each layer separately, the magnetic attachment system enhances interactivity and engagement, fostering a deeper understanding of Earth's composition and dynamics. This is a low-profile microphone arm that swivels underneath a monitor to save space. I've been using this for over 3 months, and it's been rock-solid. Fully 3D printed with no supports! All printed hardware can be swapped with M10 x 30mm bolts and M10 nuts. Clamps onto 35mm diameter poles (e.g. Ergotron or Amazon Basics monitor arms). If you don't have an existing pole, model files for a pole are provided. Included mounts for Audio Technica AT2020 microphones, ⅝"-27 threads, and ⅜"-16 threads. Magnetic cable management channel with 4mm x 2mm magnets (24 magnets required). STEP files available for purchase on Printables . Instructions Material: PETG/ABS recommended. PLA is acceptable, but creeps/deforms under constant loads more than other materials. Wall loops: 5. The arm needs to be very rigid. Infill: 15% Gyroid. Fill Multiline: 2. Nuts and bolts should be printed solid with 100% infill. Layer height: 0.20mm. Line width: 0.60mm recommended. Thicker line widths improve layer adhesion and overhang angles. 0.40mm is acceptable. Print orientation: Arms printed face up. Joint printed upside-down against the flat angle. Bolts printed along the flat cutout. Supports: None for most pieces. The ⅜" and ⅝" mic adapters require supports for the threads. Print 2 of the M10 hex tools to help tighten bolts. Assemble according to the below image. 2 nuts are required for the swivel piece to prevent rotational motion from loosening the joint--tighten the first nut to the desired tension then lock the tension with the second nut. Troubleshooting If the second arm doesn't fit into the swivel joint and can't be forced in: decrease the X-Y contour compensation of the swivel joint piece and print again. This joint is made to be a very tight interference fit to prevent sagging, so decrease this value as little as you can. If the second arm sags downwards: tighten the bolt connecting the second arm to the joint as much as you can. You may need to use pliers/wrenches to get more torque. If the swivel joint is rotating on its own: the first nut is too loosely or the second “jam nut” isn't installed. This should be tensioned such that friction overcomes gravity. If the nuts/bolts cannot handle the torque: ensure that the bolts are printed horizontally and at 100% infill. Try anything to improve layer adhesion (e.g. slower printing, higher temperatures). If the threads don't last, try lowering the line width and/or layer height to improve the print resolution. If the arm permanently creeps/deforms: this is expected with any plastic experiencing a load over time, especially since this is a long lever arm. You should be able to tighten any joints to increase the friction so gravity doesn't affect the usability of the arm even if it's deformed.

model_name: Floating Mage Tower - Magnetic Levitation Light
description: This decorative tower users the Magnetic Levitation Kit to ‘magically’ float the top portion above the base. This is my first model using this new kit and I think it provides a fun effect! Although it takes a little practice to accurately place the floating portion, no soldering is required and assembly is otherwise quite easy with no soldering required! Printed Parts Tower Base Tower Top Tower Lid Light Diffuser Banner Pegs Vine Jig Banner Jig Banners (4) Small Vines (2) Large Vines (2) Assembly Instructions The banners and vines are only 1 layer thick which means that extra care is required to remove them from the build plate. I like to use a plastic blade to work these pieces off of the plate. Optionally, you can deform pieces using the included jigs. For the vines, place then into the slots in the jig and use a hair dryer or other heat source to gently deform them to the shape. For the banners, clip them to the included jig and deform them as in the previous step. You may need to press lightly to deform the banners into the valleys of the jig. Remove the levitation float, power supply coil and light board from their protective shell. Be very cautious with the coil as it is fragile. Make sure to keep the plastic spacer between the float and coil - you will use it later. Place the power coil into the space at the bottom of the Tower Top. Bend the wire to the light board so that it's out of the way and aligned to the gaps in the side. Although not pictured, place the spacer on top of the coil. Press the levitation float into the base and bend the wire to the light board so that it sits on top. Place the light diffuser over the light board - it should sit loosely in place. Place the small vines into the Tower Top using the attached pegs. Insert the (4) banner pegs into the Tower Top (note that they should be rotated so that the clips are nearest each other with the gap facing down and then insert the (2) banners into the gaps. You may want to use a small amount of glue to hold the banners in place. Remove the top protective shell from the magnetic levitation base. Be sure to keep the bottom protective shell - you'll use it in the next step! Attach a puck light to the bottom of the magnetic levitation base shell using the included adhesive patch. Adjust the nut on the female end of the power cord so that it fits snugly into the slot on the tower base. Align the light switch panel into the slot with the smooth side facing outward. Place the magnetic levitation base into the Tower Base, aligning to each of the 4 corners. Press the tower lid onto the base. Levitation Tips Lower the top directly down onto the base after the power is plugged in. Keep a finger between the two parts so that they don't snap together and cause damage. Observe the float from a low perspective to identify if it is balanced. Imbalance may cause the top to rotate more than desired. Look for low spots that are consistent and mark them. To balance the top, I used putty in the interior of the top to slightly adjust the weight. The levitation base should be very close to the lid when closed - almost touching. If the base isn't this close, the top won't be able to float. Note in this photo how high the base is before the lid is attached. Printing Tips Note the settings for the Tower Top in the included profile - this piece is intentionally printed very thin and light so that it can levitate evenly. Profiles are included for A1 and A1 mini but note that I have tested this print on a P1S. Additional supports may be required for the Tower Top piece for A1 and A1 mini if you have challenges with them staying attached. AMS is helpful but not required. If you don't have AMS, just separate the banners from the other plates and print them in a single color. You can customize the banner using the MakerLab Make My Sign tools. If using a 0.4mm nozzle, ensure that each piece of the sign is 0.2mm tall so that it prints in a single layer. This helps it be thin enough to deform with heat. Optionally, I like to add a negative part in Bambu Studio to add a scalloped shape to the bottom of the banner. As photographed, this model was printed in PLA and painted with acrylics.

Customizable foldable box Se desiderate una versione più adatta a regali utilizzatte il mio nuovo moldello “foldable gift box”, da pochi giorni presente nel mio profilo! Il modello è ispirato alle invenzioni del celebre inventore Robert Gair, che nel 1890 realizzò i primi esempi di scatole pieghevoli destinate all’utilizzo industriale. Questa versione rappresenta una rivisitazione parametrica del concetto originale, con numerose modifiche volte a rendere funzionali la maggior parte delle misure. La stampa delle scatole con questo metodo offre diversi vantaggi; tra i principali si distinguono il significativo risparmio di filamento e la possibilità di ottenere una texture su tutti i lati del modello. Una volta completata la stampa, il pezzo necessita esclusivamente di essere piegato lungo le scanalature predisposte. Dimensioni del modello Altezza: parametro “height” Larghezza e profondità: parametri “side a; side b" Caratteristiche di stampa Il modello è stato realizzato utilizzando una A1 Mini ed è compatibile con tutte le stampanti 3D di fascia medio-alta e alta. Il progetto è stato sviluppato interamente in Fusion 360 e ha richiesto la realizzazione di circa 65 prototipi , al fine di garantire la massima funzionalità e resistenza. Non sono necessari supporti e il modello si stampa completamente piatto. Il modello deve essere piegato manualmente dopo la stampa, tenendo il lato a contatto sul piatto esterno. Nota personale La realizzazione di questo progetto è stata particolarmente impegnativa: era la prima volta che affrontavo la progettazione di un modello interamente parametrico e inizialmente non avevo idea del numero di formule necessarie per farlo funzionare correttamente. Nonostante ciò, sono molto soddisfatto del risultato finale. Dopo numerosi tentativi, le tolleranze risultano corrette e le scatole ottenute presentano un aspetto solido e decisamente professionale. *le immagini di copertina sono render, con lo scopo di presentare il modello, la versione effettiva potrebbe leggermente variare. Lista aggiornamenti: V1- 21/12/2025 V2 - 30/12/2025: sistema di chiusura migliorato V3 - 21/01/2026: completo rifacimento del modello per ottimizzarlo e renderlo più stabile. Inoltre, sono stati modificati alcuni dei parametri generativi del sistema di chiusura, che ora costruiscono il modello su basi geometriche e pertanto risultano perfettamente a filo, rendendo la chiusura molto più resistente. E' stato corretto il problema delle pareti oblique, che risultavano leggermente inclinate anche nella parte superiore, ora sono quasi perfettamente perpendicolari e complanari con il tappo chiuso. Zkull Layered Sculpture The Zkull Layered Sculpture is a skull sculpture conceived as a graphic landscape, built not as a solid volume but as a succession of vertical layers that draw the form in fragments. Each slice becomes a line of drawing in space, and together they create a silhouette that is sharp, architectural, and hypnotic. Depending on the version, the Zkull Layered Sculpture completely changes personality: in matte white , it looks like a minimalist, almost museum-like monolith, with a very subtle play of shadows between the layers; in psychedelic multicolor , the slices turn into a chromatic wave, creating a vibrant optical effect that shifts with the viewing angle. Somewhere between digital art, parametric design, and contemporary home decor, the Zkull Layered Sculpture is designed as a statement piece: a graphic totem that instantly catches the eye, whether displayed on a desk, a shelf, or showcased on its stand like a small gallery sculpture. Technical Guidelines Layer Height: 0.20 mm Perimeters (Walls): 2–3 Infill: 10–20% (increase for load-bearing parts) Top/Bottom Layers: 4 Supports: Use the provided orientations, Bambu Studio and the included profiles handle them efficiently Temperatures: Keep the default profile values or adjust slightly to match your filament Material: Bambu Lab Matte PLA Assembly & Handling Recommendations When removing the skull head from the build plate, lift it gently. The layered plates are well attached, but they remain delicate by nature. During assembly, always support the layers with your hand positioned as flat as possible across the surface, perpendicular to the layers, to avoid bending or stressing the thin plates. Once the connector pins are aligned and inserted, apply a small amount of strong glue to the main central rod. Bring the two halves together firmly but without excessive pressure to avoid damaging the layered structure. The stand should be printed with a higher infill (as indicated in the included file settings) to ensure the sculpture sits securely and isn’t top-heavy. If you notice slight misalignment between a few layers after assembling both halves, this may be caused by tiny leftover strands of filament under the base of the skull, which can interfere with the support cylinder and shift a plate. Simply clean any remaining filament carefully and realign.

description: Bring the Dark Side to your workbench with this 3D printable model of Darth Vader’s TIE Advanced x1 , as seen in Star Wars: A New Hope . This model is designed for detailed display and satisfying assembly, making it perfect for fans, collectors, and makers alike. Assembly Required: This is a glue-together model with multiple parts for better quality and ease of printing. Assembly Aids Included: Comes with helper tools to make assembly easier and more precise. Uses Filament as Pins: You’ll need short pieces of 1.75mm filament (cut to 16mm) for joining key components. Wing Assembly Tool doubles as a gauge for cutting 1.75mm filament pins to the correct 16mm length. Designed with AMS/MMU compatibility in mind, but also fully printable in single-color setups. Whether you're building your own Imperial fleet or just love detailed model kits, this print brings Vader’s legendary starfighter to life on your shelf. Assembly Notes: Glue is required for final assembly. Use 1.75mm filament cut to 16mm for joining parts (tool included to measure pins). Print the included wing alignment tool for easier and cleaner construction. Recommended layer height: 0.16–0.2 mm Use the provided tool to shape the inner wing panels (CENTER_IN): Apply a small amount of glue to the seams. Bend the top and bottom sections into place and place the panel in the tool while the glue sets. While the inner panel dries, prepare the solar panel inserts (WING_TOP and WING_BOTTOM): Insert the solar panels into the top and bottom outer wing skins. Optionally, glue the panels in place to prevent them from falling out. Attach the outer center section (CENTER_OUT): Insert the small panel (RAD_CENTER_FRONT) in the front and the longer panel (RAD_CENTER_REAR) in the back. Note: The longer panel only has one correct orientation. Flip it if it doesn’t align. Use the wing assembly tool to glue the outer skins (WING_TOP and WING_BOTTOM) to the inner panel (CENTER_IN): Apply glue evenly to the edges of the inner panel. Align the solar panels with their corresponding holes. Clamp the pieces together while the glue dries. Repeat these steps for the other wing assembly. model_name: Hidden furniture panel connector with marking tool
description: A way to connect furniture panels without visible screws. This connector snaps plywood, mdf or melamine panels together tightly. It includes a marking jig for positioning both the puck and the snapper at the right distance from the edge of the material. The puck (round part) and the snapper are designed to be used with 4x16 screws. The marking jig requires longer screws, I used 4x20 but longer is also possible. First, drive two screws through the jig so that the points protrude just a tiny bit. This marks the panel where the snapper goes. Then, mark on the edge of the material where you want the connector. Position the jig at the desired location and put a puck in the jig. Screw down the puck and the jig now stays attached to the puck. Lastly, hold the panel you want to attach in front of the other panel and press against the jig to mark two screw locations. Attach the snapper with two screws. Now simply push the panel in and it snaps shut!

Join my membership The Ultimate DMs Kit I've taken the portability of the Ultimate Players Kit and scaled it majorly to form the Ultimate DMs kit! Two boxes form storage for everything you could need to run a session. The kit comes in two halves, each folds up to become a portable carrying case, with enough room to fit your entire kit, and when its assembled and unpacked it turns into a stunning setpiece for your games. Customizable Storage Each box is big enough to store 2 standard DND books or you can add in the available inserts for minis shelves or drawers to keep all of your kit organized. Features Hidden magnets inside each door panel, letting you hang up session notes or DM guides A4 paper storage - Each door panel can fit up to 20 pages per door! Store your notes, or extra character sheets Built in initiative tracking - Each door contains extra magnetic panels to allow you to quickly add initiative order Dual Dice Towers - One facing the DM for private rolls, and another facing the players for public rolls Customizable shelf inserts - add shelves or drawers to suit your DM style. Securely store your kit - Each side folds together and clips closed securely with latches Portability - each side has a handle for easy carrying, and the handle is long enough that both sides can easily be carried together in one hand. No AMS required. All decorations are assembled as parts and so the entire kit can be printed with or without an AMS unit. Snap together construction - most of the kit can be built with just the included snap connectors Materials Needed Super glue 4x M3x20 socket head bolts and nuts 6x 20x3mm magnets 28 6x3mm magnets for the hidden magnetic panels - you can use less if you only want certain spots to be magnetic 26 6x3mm magnets for the initiative tracking - you can use less if you don't want initiative tracking or only want one side to be magnetic. Print Profile Settings Please use the print profiles provided if possible. They have been tested on multiple slicers and should work for most klipper based slicers. There are a lot of per-object customizations that have been done, and a heap of manually painted supports, especially on the dice towers. Mostly I use standard print profile settings. 0.2mm layer heights Support Overhang Threshold: 23% - This stops supports from generating inside the dice tower Supports on build plate only Critical supports only Print orientation: Most decorative panels should be printed vertically, so add a 10mm brim to the outside to keep it grounded. Print with the connection holes facing up so that if there are warping issues it doesn't affect joints. Note: The dice tower and tower door is the only thing that should need supports, everything else should have supports disabled as they aren't needed and unnecessarily slow down printing. The overhangs for almost every decorative piece have been designed to not need to be supported (45 degree angles etc) but the brickwork sometimes tricks the slicer into thinking you need it, so I would recommend just disabling it except for the dice tower and the dice tower door. Assembly The kit is designed to be assembled mostly with snap together clips, though some glue will be needed for the dice towers and for the extra decorative panels. Assembly Video A full build of one half of the tower can be found here: https://www.instagram.com/reel/DXUmJ0gCdIB/?utm_source=ig_web_copy_link&igsh=MzRlODBiNWFlZA== Step 1 - Assemble the dice tower Using a bit of glue on each of the towers pegs, build the dice tower. Insert the dice door into the door frame at the bottom String a piece of filament through the holes at the bottom through the door hinge. Note: the door may need some minor adjustments to fit - different filaments print at different sizes and you may need to sand back the door frame a little to get the fit you want. Step 2 - Assemble the main box Start by assembling the main box frame together - be concious of making sure each side is upright (the edge with the connector holes are both facing up) Using the included double sided connectors, and the connector insertion tool (included in each profile), insert snap connectors into the main box frame. Once the connectors are in one side, I find that connecting the side with the connectors to the sides with the receivers is made easier with a few light taps with a small hammer. Add the snap connectors around the permiter of the main box frame Using snap connectors, assemble the front facing panels (castle walls), again I find light tapping with a hammer to be very effective in joining the two halves. Lay the facade onto the frame, making sure that the the correct side is up (the side of the box frame with the handle hinges is facing upward, and press fit the frames snaps into the facades snap receivers. Add decorations. Using a bit of super glue, add the decorations to the main box castle face - the door and the two rounded windows. Add in 20mm magnets to the inset circles on the side, making sure that the polarity matches the correct direction so the boxes join together Using the m3 bolts, add the handle to the top of the box. Step 3 - Join Main Box to Dice Tower. Slide in the two dovetailed threaded slides into the approriate place in the dice tower taking care to ensure one threaded hole is at the top and the other is at the bottom. Optionally, add a drop or two of glue to the dovetail inserts for a more secure assembly Line up the main box with the threaded holes, and using the included printed bolts screw the two panels together. Don't over tighten the bolts or you risk snapping them Tip: I've found it sometimes easier to drive the bolts through the threaded holes while disassembled to allow the two parts to break eachother in before assembling. Step 4 - Build the Door panels Similarly to the main box, the door panels are all joined using the snap connectors. Start by joining the inner top panel to the inner bottom panel. A few light taps with a hammer can help here as well. Optionally - add the magnets to the inside of the inner panel, taking care to maintain the polarity the same for each magnet you add. These magnets should seat lower than the opening, so make sure they sink all the way to the bottom. Add in snap connectors around the perimeter of the inner panel Assemble the Outer Panels Join the assembled outer panels to the inner panel Optionally - add magnets to the initiative tracking section of the outer panel Using a bit of super glue, add the window decorations to the outer panel. Step 5 - Join the door panels to the dice tower Using a long piece of filament, line up the door panel to the hinges on the dice tower and carefully thread the filament through to form the hinge. You may need to lift and adjust the door as you are passing the filament through to clear the pathway, but you should be able to get filament all the way through. Optionally - apply a little heat to the end of the filament hinge to secure it in. Add the door latches to the door panel, making sure the latch is facing the right direction. Step 6 - Customize Insert whatever shelves you want or drawers and get ready for your next session! Other tips for success Please use the print profiles provided if possible. They have been tested on multiple slicers and should work for most klipper based slicers. There are a lot of per-object customizations that have been done, and a heap of manually painted supports, especially on the dice towers. Check and double check your slicer results before you hit print. A little bit of advanced checking can save heaps of filament. This is a big project, and each half uses ~1.3kg of filament, so make sure you know that going in you will need ~2.5kg of your main filament. Please note going into this: this is a serious build. It's not difficult by any means but it does take like an hour to build so be prepared for that in advance Special Thanks A special thanks to my makerworld subscribers and especially discord user McMike who put in some serious hours and filament beta testing this!

Though this version is merely inspired by automatic generation techniques, it allows for precise control of wall angles, reducing the need for extensive supports. I trust everyone is in good spirits. I'm contacting you because I'm encountered increasing difficulties displaying my work on Facebook and, more so, on Reddit. Although I'm utilizing this platform and others, I'm seeking alternative methods to show my work. A community member ( Kardes.Design ) suggested an abominations called "TikTok", which I admit I've previously attempted with limited success. Nevertheless, I'm willing to try again to share my development journey and updates. For TikTok users, you can find me at: www.tiktok.com/@designrepcom . Your support in sharing would be greatly valued. And here a tiny clip for this project Context This mouse has been constructed in a completely different manner from previous versions, with a particular focus on functional and ergonomic aspects. Think of it as a study rather than the final product. Nevertheless, I have decided to release it for those interested in experimenting. What to expect: Optimal comfort level for a hand size within the 90th percentile, which includes most adult male hands. Perfect button actuation. Given the button layout in this kit, as well as the limitations imposed by 3D printing, this will be the most suitable key configuration and should work with most printing configurations. A little bit of the design process - Prototype creation (2th iteration on the make) I have included a version with specific material for support. Especially for those with an AMS system, this is one of the materials that should always be loaded. It is true that it is somewhat expensive, but if used only on the interface layer, this material will allow for many prints, as only a small amount is used on the contact zone. The advantage is an almost perfect interface zone. Bambu Lab currently offers " Support for PLA ," which is a relatively elastic material with very low adhesion to the piece's walls. PVA , which is water-soluble, can also be used and allows for even superior results. Both are excellent options. The downside is that the printing will take much longer to complete, and the purging effect will consume some of the precious support material. You can also try using PETG as a support material. Since the melting temperatures of the two materials are similar, they are incompatible (they don't "fuse" together), which is beneficial for support structures. However, PVA or the specific support material allows for superior results, and in terms of configurations, everything is automated in Bambu Studio. For those interested in understanding the development process of this and other products, which, as you can see, originated from a sculpture to ensure the most ergonomic design possible, the object was then 3D scanned . And you know what? It's something everyone should try. Simply printing pieces that others have made is just one part of the experience, a small part, not bad, but only a fraction of the experience, if you like to print you should try create something. So, I invite everyone to give it a try. Start by taking the first step: create a simple model using the CAD tool of your choice, or make a clay sculpture, or a model of what you want (I often start with these). What matters is to begin. You already have one thing mastered: printing. Now, just take one more step to become a creator. Jorge Rui

description: VERTICAL RACE Scalatori pronti… si parte! Questo gioco da tavolo stampabile in 3D porta l’emozione dell’arrampicata sportiva direttamente sulla tua scrivania. Sfida un amico a chi raggiunge per primo la cima della parete: serviranno tattica, fortuna e un pizzico di competizione! Il modello completo raggiunge i 40 cm di altezza una volta assemblato, ma non preoccuparti: non è necessario alcun AMS per la stampa. Tutte le parti sono ottimizzate per la stampa in singoli colori. Il gioco è pensato per tutte le età , anche per i più piccoli, ed è perfetto per divertirsi in famiglia o con gli amici. Caratteristiche principali: Design originale e divertente Facile da stampare e montare Ideale come progetto ludico-educativo 🛠️ Assemblaggio: Una volta stampati tutti i pezzi, segui questi semplici passaggi per assemblare il tuo gioco: Unisci i due pezzi principali della parete di arrampicata. L’incastro è intuitivo, ma per una maggiore stabilità si consiglia un punto di colla cianoacrilica lungo le giunture interne. Incolla le prese negli appositi incavi seguendo con attenzione il seguente schema colorato. Questo passaggio è fondamentale per mantenere la coerenza del percorso e garantire l’equilibrio tra i due giocatori. Monta la ruota girevole (utilizzata per determinare le mosse di gioco) secondo il seguente schema di assemblaggio. Assicurati che il perno centrale consenta una rotazione fluida, senza eccessivo attrito. 🎲 Istruzioni del gioco: Vertical Race è un gioco di strategia e azione: l’obiettivo è raggiungere per primi la vetta della parete con il proprio scalatore. Ma attenzione! Più appigli utilizzi, più sicura sarà la tua salita… ma anche più lenta. Rischierai o giocherai sul sicuro? PUNTO DI PARTENZA: Posizionare la parete di arrampicata tra i due giocatori in modo che ognuno si trovi da un lato del pannello. Ogni giocatore sceglie il proprio scalatore del proprio colore. Inizia la partica il giocatore con meno esperienza nell’arrampicata sportiva. Il primo scalatore gira la ruota: in base al colore uscito, può inserire il primo perno delle mani nella presa del colore corrispondente, mantenendo i piedi dello scalatore a contatto con il terreno. Poi tocca al secondo giocatore, che compie la stessa azione. Da questo momento, la scalata ha inizio: scegli con attenzione il percorso e muoviti con strategia! LA SCALATA: Ogni giocatore si muove come un vero scalatore: i movimenti devono rispettare la logica dell’arrampicata verticale (mai a testa in giù!). Le braccia devono sempre restare sopra le gambe. Se lo scalatore è appeso solo con un braccio o una gamba, il movimento successivo deve coinvolgere un arto diverso. Altrimenti, cade. In caso di caduta, lo scalatore deve ripartire dal basso. Se uno scalatore è bloccato (con entrambe le braccia e almeno una gamba fissate) e non può più salire, può liberare un arto a scelta. In questo caso, perde il turno. Questa azione può essere ripetuta ogni volta che è necessario. IL VINCITORE: Vince il primo giocatore che riesce a portare il proprio scalatore fino alla vetta. La scalata si considera completata quando lo scalatore tocca con una mano una delle due bandiere in cima alla parete. LA RUOTA: Colore singolo : puoi muovere una mano o un piede del tuo scalatore verso una presa del colore indicato. Se non puoi fare alcuna mossa e decidi di non fissare i piedi, perdi il turno. Multicolore : Che fortuna! Puoi muovere qualunque arto verso il colore che preferisci. Caduta massi : Sfortuna! Lo scalatore non può muoversi per un turno. 🔥 Variante Avanzata – Doppia Arrampicata Vuoi aumentare il livello di sfida? Prova la modalità con due scalatori per giocatore! In questa versione, ogni giocatore controlla due scalatori contemporaneamente. Le regole di base restano le stesse, ma con alcune modifiche: Ogni giocatore effettua due movimenti a turno, uno per ciascuno dei propri scalatori. Può decidere l’ordine liberamente. I due scalatori non possono occupare la stessa presa contemporaneamente. Se uno dei due scalatori cade, riparte da terra, ma l’altro può continuare la scalata. Vince il primo giocatore che riesce a portare entrambi i suoi scalatori in cima, ognuno toccando una bandiera diversa. Ora hai tutto quello che ti serve per iniziare la sfida! Che tu scelga la modalità classica o quella avanzata con due scalatori, Vertical Race ti farà mettere alla prova riflessi, logica e sangue freddo… proprio come su una vera parete di arrampicata!

model_name: Math Learning Cylinder - Tablas de Multiplicar
description: ## 🧮 Interactive Multiplication Cylinder Learning math has never been so satisfying! This cylinder is a handheld mechanical calculator designed to help students and children memorize the multiplication tables from 1 to 10 interactively. ### How does it work? The design consists of an outer casing with the numbers 1 through 10 (multiplicand) and a rotating lower ring (multiplier). By rotating the lower ring to select a number, the correct multiplication results magically appear in the vertical slot. ### ⚠ Important Requirements * MULTICOLOR ONLY: This design requires a multi-color unit (AMS, MMU, etc.). The numbers are integrated into the vertical geometry and cannot be painted on with a simple filament change by height adjustment. * Print-in-Place: The mechanism is printed pre-assembled. Once printing is complete, simply rotate the ring with a little initial force to break any minimal adhesion, and it will begin to rotate smoothly. ### ⚙ Recommended Print Settings * Material: PLA (Recommended for better tolerance). * Supports: NO (Disable them completely). * Layer Height: 0.20mm (Works well; you can lower it to 0.16mm for more precise measurements). * Infill: 15% (Grid or Gyroid). * Brim: Usually not necessary if you have good adhesion, but use it if you're worried about it coming loose. I hope you like it and that it helps many little geniuses learn math! Don't forget to upload your makes! ## 🧮 Cilindro de Multiplicar Interactivo ¡Aprender matemáticas nunca fue tan satisfactorio! Este cilindro es una calculadora mecánica manual diseñada para ayudar a estudiantes y niños a memorizar las tablas de multiplicar del 1 al 10 de forma interactiva. ### ¿Cómo funciona? El diseño consta de una carcasa exterior con los números del 1 al 10 (multiplicando) y un anillo giratorio inferior (multiplicador). Al girar el anillo inferior para seleccionar un número, los resultados correctos de la multiplicación aparecen mágicamente en la ranura vertical. ### ⚠ Requisitos Importantes * SOLO MULTICOLOR: Este diseño requiere una unidad multicolor (AMS, MMU, etc.). Los números están integrados en la geometría vertical y no se pueden pintar con un simple cambio de filamento por altura. * Print-in-Place: El mecanismo se imprime ya ensamblado. Una vez finalizada la impresión, solo tienes que girar el anillo con un poco de fuerza inicial para romper la mínima adherencia y empezará a girar suavemente. ### ⚙ Configuración de Impresión Recomendada * Material: PLA (Recomendado para mejor tolerancia). * Soportes: NO (Desactívalos completamente). * Altura de capa: 0.20mm (Funciona bien, puedes bajar a 0.16 para números más definidos). * Relleno: 15% (Grid o Gyroid). * Borde (Brim): No suele ser necesario si tienes buena adherencia, pero úsalo si temes que se despegue. ¡Espero que os guste y ayude a muchos pequeños genios a aprender mates! PipeLink Chainmail Fabric - Square Chainmail with a Twist PipeLink Chainmail Fabric is a modern twist on traditional chainmail, and on similar 3d printed designs. While modeling the chamfered links I was reminded of classic pipeline mobile games, hence the name of this project. Unlike previously released square chainmail projects, I have modified both the typical direction of the weave, as well as adding unique edge geometry. A Note Of Caution: Please note that the difficulty in achieving a successful print will increase with the size if fabric you select. Printing a 16-576 piece of chainmail is easier than the 1,296 piece version. Before you attempt to print larger versions I highly recommend the following: Use a build plate with good adhesion that has been properly washed and cleaned . I have successfully printed this design on both Supertack and Textured PEI plates. Dial-in the settings for the filament you are using. If the first layer isn't perfect, the nozzle can easily catch stray plastic and destroy the print on subsequent layers due to the minimal adhesion surfaces. Print smaller versions and correct any issues before printing larger versions. No one likes wasting filament on test prints, which is why the ‘Tiny’ and ‘Small’ test prints both have keyrings attached to them - it's a test print & a keyring! (Both sizes pictured above.) Use Bed Leveling & Automatic Flow Dynamics Calibration… I know, I know, I leave these off for most prints to save time, but they really will help this print succeed. Don't despair if you encounter a print failure. There is some inherent difficulty in achieving a successful print of a large model with minimal adhesion surfaces. I assure you that the print profiles I have provided will produce good results if you take the time to follow the above recommendations. Additionally, filament matters. While you may be able to print this in TPU, PETG, or any number of more exotic options, I have only printed this with basic PLA and Polymaker PLA Pro. Feel free to upload your own unique print profile if you find something that works great for you. Various Print Profiles: I've included two basic print profiles in this project. Each profile has 7 plates, each with increasingly large sizes. Here's a brief description of the plate sizes and profiles: Every Profile Has These 7 Plates: Tiny (4x4) Keyring : A 14-minute print, perfect for testing, and it's a keyring so the print isn't a waste. Small (8x8) Keyring : Double the tiny fun at 35-minutes to print, it's also a keyring so the print isn't a waste. Intermediate (12x12) : A 1-hour 12-minute print, 3-inch square panel. Medium (18x18) : A 2-hour 32-minute print, perfect 4.5-inch square fidget size. (Pictured above.) Big (24x24) : A 4-hour 25-minute print, 6-inch square panel. Bigger (30x30) : A 6-hour 47-minute print, it's a bigger than big at 7.5-inches square. Humongous (36x36) : A whopping 9-hour 42-minute print, because sometimes, biggest really is better! This takes up nearly the entire build plate. (Pictured in cover photo). Choose A Profile: PipeLink Chainmail (One Color) - I would recommend at least printing the ‘Tiny’ plate to test your printer before moving on to one of the larger plates. If Tiny prints well you should be able to print at least up to ‘Big’ without any issues. PipeLink Chainmail (Two Colors) - Same as above but with a color change halfway through for an interesting effect. Special Requests: I've had a few special requests for custom modifications to this project. If you have a good idea I'm happy to see if I can make it happen. Feel free to leave a comment or message me directly. INTRODUCTION Before 3D printing, I was deeply immersed in the world of photography. Back then, if I needed something (anything) for my camera, the only option for me was to head to a photography store. Every accessory, every part, had to be purchased from those specialized shops. And if I wanted something unique that wasn’t off-the-shelf… tough luck. Customization? A dream, unless you own your own milling or CNC machine. Things have changed so much. Now with a 3D printer and some CAD skills, I can design and print the parts I need. MOCA is a combo of my 2 passions. it is a 3D-printed mobile phone cage that’s easy to print, assemble, and customize. Perfect for makers of all levels. You can choose to print in your favourite colour and add accessories to the NATO rail, creating a phone cage that’s uniquely yours. BILL OF MATERIAL FOR MOCA Sourcing parts individually can be time-consuming and tedious. To simplify this, I’ve partnered with MakerWorld’s MakerSupply to offer a MOCA/MOCA+ Hardware Kit at their store ( TBA ). If you prefer to source the hardware separately, a detailed list of parts is provided in the Assembly Guide. FILAMENT USE FOR MOCA MOCA was tested and printed using BambuLab PETG HF and PLA Basic filaments. If you're considering purchasing Bambu Lab filaments for this project, I would encourage you to use ModBotArmy's afflink . Doing so won’t cost you anything extra, but it directly supports his channel, allowing him to continue creating valuable, informative content that benefits the 3D printing community. CREDITS The MOCA project would not have been possible without the support of both companies and individuals who have helped me throughout this journey. I want to take a moment to express my sincere thanks to those who played a role in bringing this project to life. Bambu Lab – For their generous sponsorship of filaments and H2D, enabling the development and testing of MOCA. Maker Supply - For seeing the value of MOCA project and working with me to provide a Maker's kit on their store. Friends & Community – Special thanks to 247printing, Modbot, Nisha, Kane, and others for their valuable feedback, which continues to help refine the design. Spammington – Designer of the Ultimate Smartphone Mount, whose work inspired the mobile clamp portion of MOCA. CONCLUSION To date, all my designs are free to download for personal use—no Patreon, memberships, clubs, subscriptions, or bullshit. If you enjoy my designs and want to support my coffee addiction or help fund materials for prototyping, here’s how you can contribute: Share your makes in the comments or on 3D printing social media. Give a MakerWorld boost. Your support is greatly appreciated! CAVEAT As with all my designs, prototyping and testing were conducted to ensure printability and meet my standards. However, results may vary, and I cannot guarantee it will work for you. Please read all instructions carefully before printing and proceed at your own discretion.

Figure 1. 12 and 8 piece "Point Break toys" Point Break - Desk Toy I am happy to share the Point Break Desk Toy , a stylish and mesmerizing addition to your office desk , or a physics toy to put anywhere in your home. This self resetting rotational chain reaction mechanism creates a moving wave and has been named ”Point Break” after the location where waves break when hitting land. (I have now learned that this toy goes by the name Xylo by David C. Roy .) The model is available in 2 different versions (” 100% printed ” and ” Ball bearings ”) and 2 different sizes ( 8 pieces and 12 pieces ). In my opinion, the 8 piece desk toy is a nice and reasonable print while the 12 piece is more impressive but quite large. The ”100% printed” works very well and is easier to assemble . However, it does have some wobble in the X-axis. In contrast, the ”Ball bearings” version (which requires 8 or 12 “ 605ZZ STEEL EA015 Ball Bearings” or other bearings with an 14mm diameter, 5mm hole and 5mm thick), is more work to assemble but locks the rotating pieces in the X-axis and creates a much smoother, stable and satisfying movement. Printing 4 print profiles are available (100% printed – 8 pieces, 100% printed - 12 pieces, Ball bearings – 8 pieces, Ball bearings - 12 pieces). The print profiles have been organized to fit the A1 mini ( if printed in single colour or without prime tower ) and to include a modifier to add a second colour to the rotating bars. I welcome the community to provide additional profiles with different colour schemes, or plate layout. There should be no issues printing the pieces needed for this model, except for the fact that the long shape of most pieces might make them prone to warping . In addition, the small ”spacers” for the ”Ball bearing” version has little contact with the bed, so overall good bed adhesion is recommended . The bar holding the rotating pieces will be under a light constant load, and I have noticed that for the large ”12 piece version”, PLA will start creeping (bending) relatively quickly while PETG seems fine. This piece should therefore be printed in another filament like PETG or ASA . The smaller ” 8 piece” version seems fine in PLA (this far) but if you have other filaments available, use them. In addition, this piece needs to be perfectly printed for the mechanism or assembly to work. Assembly ”100% printed version” First assemble the stand by simply pressing the ”pillars” into the sockets of the ”bottom” H-shaped part (Figure 2A). This might require some force, and they should klick right into place creating a strong connection. If they for some reason are loose after pushed into place, addition of glue would probably help. Next, line up all the ”rotational pieces as in the picture (Figure 2B), and insert the rod (Figure 2C). Next put the rod into the the stand first on one side (Figure 2D) and then on the other (Figure 2E). This requires that you slightly bend the stand apart which is fine. The only thing to keep in mind is that the orientation of the pieces as one side of the ”pillars” has an extension to keep the ”rotating bars” away from it. On the other side, the ”rotating bar” itself has this extension. For it to work properly, friction needs to be as low as possible, and for this reason adding some lubricant might be a good idea (although not required in my experience). Figure 2. A) Push the long bars into the bottom stand. B) Line up all rotating rods and C) insert the Bar. D) Insert the assembly first on one side and then E) the other. ”Ball Bearing version” The stand is first assembled as the ”100% printed version” (see above). Push ball bearings into rotational pieces (Figure 3A-B). Next, organize the pieces as in the picture (Figure 3C), starting with one ”spacer ring” and then alternating ”rotational piece” with ”spacer ring”. The ”rod” now needs to be inserted (Figure 3D). Now, this should be difficult as we want the ball bearings to sit firmly in place on the rod. If it feels impossible, you could slightly sand the rod to make it thinner. The ”spacers” are not strictly required if the ball bearings are firmly secured on the ”rod”, but will still help creating an even distance between the ”rotational rods”. When assembled, simply fasten the assembly into the stand (Figure 3E). Figure 3. A-B) Insert ball bearing into slot by pressing hard. C) Line up all rotating rods and D) insert the Bar. E) Push the assembly into the stand. You should now have an mesmerizing toy for your office desk to fidget with all day instead of doing work! Please Enjoy! model_name: Parametric Generator: Flex TPU Bellows & Sleeves
description: FLEX-BELLOWS: Advanced Parametric TPU Bellows & Sleeves Generator Protect your mechanics with industrial-grade flexible covers, perfectly tailored to your projects! Introducing FLEX-BELLOWS , much more than a simple dust cover creator. This powerful parametric generator (powered by OpenSCAD) is the perfect solution for robotics, CNC machines, automotive applications, and advanced DIY. Finding a commercial off-the-shelf bellows for discontinued vehicles, or one that fits odd diameters or misaligned axes, is often impossible. This tool solves the problem at its root, allowing you to engineer protective covers with smooth transitions, integrated flanges, and complex routing paths. FLEX-BELLOWS gives you total control over the geometry for your specific needs, ensuring mechanical performance true to your chosen material. Fully optimized for 3D printing in TPU and other flexible filaments. Key Features Advanced Spatial Geometry (Offset & Twist): This is the real game-changer of the model. Are your attachment points misaligned? No problem. The generator allows you to translate the output relative to the input (X/Y Offset) and even apply a global Twist. Ideal for complex joints in irregular spaces. Integrated Mounting Flanges: Forget glue. You can enable customizable mounting flanges on both the input and output, defining thickness, chamfers, and even the exact number and position of screw holes for a professional structural mounting. Elbows and Curves (Angled Routing): Need the tube to make a 45° or 90° turn before the bellows section begins? The system supports the insertion of parametric Elbows with customizable radii to bypass obstacles in your design. O-Ring & Zip-Tie Grooves: The cuff sections feature an advanced system for adding protruding rings or recessed Grooves. Perfect for ensuring a watertight seal with O-rings or providing a solid seat for classic zip-ties. Total Wave Profile Customization: You are not limited to the classic "zigzag". Choose between sinusoidal, triangular, trapezoidal, or scalloped profiles. Furthermore, you can apply a profile distortion (Skew) to create "sawtooth" bellows that compress preferentially in a single direction. Extreme Geometries & Transitions Support: Smoothly blends a square input into a circular output, or even complex ellipses and polygons (hexagons, octagons). The transitions between the rigid cuff walls and the thin bellows walls are mathematically calculated to eliminate stress concentration points. Examples of Generable Models Here are just a few examples of what you can create with this generator. Automotive CV Joint Boot: A bellow styled like those used for car axle shafts, designed for high flexibility and dynamic movement. Classic Cylindrical: The standard, reliable bellow featuring perfectly circular input and output cuffs. Square Input Flange: A custom design featuring a square structural mounting flange on the input side. Angled Output (Elbow): Features a circular input flange and a curved routing (elbow) on the output side to bypass structural obstacles. Elliptical Profile: Specifically designed to fit non-standard housings, with both input and output in an elliptical shape. Gear Shift Boot (Square to Circular): A smooth geometric transition from a square base to a circular top, typical of automotive manual transmission shifters. Dual Flange & Elliptical Body: A highly engineered joint featuring integrated mounting flanges on both ends, joined by a fully elliptical bellows section. 3D Printing & Customizer Guide Whether you are generating your STL file or setting up your slicer, follow these guidelines to ensure the maximum mechanical durability of your FLEX-BELLOWS: Optimization via Customizer (MakerWorld / OpenSCAD) Use the Customizer panel to input your measurements. The model includes a "Show_Cross_Section" feature to let you check internal thicknesses before exporting. The "Fast Rendering" feature leverages the Manifold engine to show you real-time changes without annoying lag! Material Recommendations TPU (Thermoplastic Polyurethane): The material of choice. A 95A TPU is perfect for rigid bellows and CNC dust boots. If you need extreme flexibility and compression, opt for a softer TPU (e.g., 85A or 82A). TPE / PCTPE: Great for applications requiring high chemical resistance (e.g., motor oils or linear guide greases). Build Plate Tip: TPU adheres incredibly well to PEI sheets. On smooth plates, consider using a glue stick—not for adhesion, but as a "release agent" to avoid damaging the bed after printing. Infill & Walls (Crucial for TPU) Bellows Wall Thickness: In the generator, the Bellows_Wall_Thickness parameter defines the wave thickness. For perfect prints, set this value as an exact multiple of your nozzle diameter (e.g., for a 0.4mm nozzle, set 0.8mm or 1.2mm). Arachne Engine: In your slicer settings, make sure the "Arachne" perimeter generator is enabled. It is essential for printing thin walls continuously without micro-retractions (which cause stringing and holes in TPU). Infill: The bellows walls will print as 100% continuous perimeters. For thicker flanges and cuffs, use a Gyroid infill at 15-25% to retain some elasticity under stress. Orientation & Supports (Crucial Slicing Note) The mathematical design of this model is intended to make your extruder's life easier: Orientation: Print the bellows vertically, placing the input or output on the build plate. Use the Base_Orientation option in the code to automatically flip the entire piece depending on which flange is wider (to get the largest contact surface on the bed). Support-Free: If you maintain reasonable geometric angles, the bellows wave will print perfectly in TPU without any internal or external supports. Enable supports (standard or tree) ONLY if you have generated 90-degree Elbows or flanges with overhanging holes. Setup & Daily Us Putting your newly printed joint to use is straightforward: Creation: Measure the hardware to be protected (e.g., rod diameter and housing diameter), input the data into the generator, download the STL, and print. Installation: Slip the bellows onto your mechanical parts. Fastening: If you generated Grooves, insert a nylon zip-tie or a rubber O-ring and tighten. If you used flanges, secure them with flat-head screws for a permanent, torsion-resistant anchor. Original Design & Media Note The 3D design was created entirely by me from scratch, specifically designed and optimized for 3D printing. Please note that while the promotional video includes some AI-generated conceptual images to illustrate the model's theme, the gallery features several real photographs showcasing the actual 3D-printed model. TrayStack ist ein kompakter Organizer für Kleinteile, Werkzeuge oder SD-Karten, der speziell für den Schreibtisch entwickelt wurde. Das gesamte System ist auf den Bauraum des A1 mini optimiert, liefert maximale Stabilität bei minimalem Materialeinsatz und folgt dem Prinzip: Form Follows Function . Nutzt gern das neue TrayStack MAX System um wirklich alles perfekt zu verstauen. Hier geht es zum TrayStack MAX System Das Konzept: Drei Ebenen. Ein Griff. Volle Kontrolle. Das System besteht aus einer Außenbox und drei perfekt abgestimmten Einsätzen: Der Base-Tray (Unten): Verfügt über einen integrierten Zentralgriff, der über die gesamte Höhe des Systems ragt. Er bildet die stabile "Wirbelsäule". Die Stack-Trays (Mitte & Oben): Dank präzise tolerierter Führungsschlitze werden die oberen Schalen einfach über den Griff gefädelt und gleiten ruckelfrei in Position. Das Handling: Wenn alle Einsätze ineinandergesteckt sind, greifst du einfach den zentralen Griff und hebst den kompletten 3-stöckigen Block mit einer Hand aus der Box oder setzt ihn wieder ein. Jeder einzelne Einsatz (Base, Mittelteil und Oberteil) existiert in 4 verschiedenen Varianten mit unterschiedlichen Tray-Größen und Fächereinteilungen. Diese wählst du dir einfach über die Plattenauswahl des entsprechenden Druckprofils aus. Egal ob du lange Stifte, winzige SMD-Bauteile, Schrauben, USB-Sticks oder Werkzeug verstauen willst - du kannst dir genau die Kombination ausdrucken, die du für deinen Workflow brauchst. Bewusste Design-Entscheidung: Keine vertikale Stapelbarkeit Ein wichtiger Hinweis zur Design-Philosophie dieses Projekts: Die Boxen sind bewusst NICHT vertikal in die Höhe stapelbar designt. Warum? Um das klare, minimalistische und funktionale Design auf dem Schreibtisch zu erhalten. Vertikale Stapelsysteme neigen bei dieser kompakten Grundfläche dazu, klobig zu wirken und den schnellen Zugriff zu blockieren. TrayStack setzt auf direkten, ergonomischen Workflow auf einer Ebene. Modulare Erweiterung: Das TrayStack Grid Du brauchst mehr Platz? Statt in die Höhe zu bauen, erweitert sich TrayStack in der Ebene. Über das TrayStack Grid kannst du das System der Länge nach modular erweitern. Mit dem Grid lassen sich mehrere Boxen nahtlos und bombenfest nebeneinander fixieren. So wächst dein Organizer-System exakt mit deinen Anforderungen, während dein Schreibtisch optisch clean und aufgeräumt bleibt. Für maximale Flexibilität beim Drucken stehen dir 3 verschiedene Grid-Komponenten zur Verfügung: Das Single-Grid: Perfekt, wenn du eine einzelne, isolierte Box sauber einfassen und ihr einen festen Stand auf dem Tisch verpassen willst. Das End-Piece (Außenseite): Der Abschluss-Gris für die Außenseitem. Wenn du exakt zwei Boxen nebeneinander nutzen willst, druckst du einfach nur zwei Stück davon. Sie werden direkt miteinander verbunden, und du kannst deine zwei Boxen hineinstellen. Das Extension-Piece (Verlängerungsteil): Das universelle Mittelstück. Hiermit kannst du deine Reihe in der Mitte beliebig oft und unendlich erweitern, um so viele Boxen nebeneinander zu stellen, wie dein Schreibtisch hergibt.

According to Uaiás mythology, Pirarucu was the son of a local chief. He was cruel and arrogant warrior who was disrespectful to the gods. As punishment, the highest of the gods, Tupan, dragged him to the bottom of the river and transformed him into the first arapaima. Arapaima gigas (also called pirarucu) is one of the largest freshwater fish in the world, reaching over 10 ft in length and weighing 220 lbs. These ancient armored fish are native to the Amazon and Essequibo River basins, but have been introduced in other tropical regions around the world. They possess a labyrinth lung (like the Northern Snakehead) allowing them to gulp air and survive in poorly oxygenated waters. They also possess scales composed of a hard mineralized outer layer on top of multiple tough layers of collagen to protect them from predators. Despite these adaptations, their numbers have been declining in their native range due to overfishing. Today, individuals longer than 6 ft are rare in the wild. The species gained more public attention when it was featured on an episode of River Monsters. Angler Jeremy Wade journeyed deep into the Amazon rainforest, racing against the looming monsoon season to find and catch an absolute monster of a fish. I was lucky enough to hook an arapaima just once but it was the fight of a lifetime. For 16 minutes all I could do was hold on as it took back what little line I was able to pull in, at no point was I in control of that fish. Then in an instant it launched half it's body above the water, shook it's head, and spat the hook. It was such a memorable experience that inspired to design this model. Assembly is the same as my other articulated fish models, push the registration pin into place, add glue to the flat piece bottoms, push the two halves together, and secure with tape. For this one though, I highly recommend adding glue to all perimeter scales, not just the head and tailfin. Happy printing!

Add a splash of gravity-defying fun to your day with this charming Penguin Roly-Poly Toy! Designed as a self-righting wobble toy, this penguin tumbles, rocks, and spins for 30+ seconds before standing right back up again. This innovative toy combines simple physics with playful interaction, creating a fun hands-on experience for all ages while also encouraging curiosity and exploration! 🧠 The Educational Aspect: Learning Through Play This toy introduces core concepts through interactive play: Cause & Effect: Early learners discover that their physical actions (a tap or push) create immediate reactions. Motor Skills: Following the 30+ second wobble improves visual tracking, while reaching for it refines hand-eye coordination. Introduction to Physics: The self-righting action naturally introduces older kids to center of gravity, balance, and momentum, sparking curiosity about how things work. ⚙️ Technical Features & Design Built to be an elegant, easy-to-print project, this model maximizes performance without relying on external parts: Enduring Motion: Precisely calibrated geometry ensures a single push creates a sustained wobble lasting over 30 seconds. Zero Hardware Required: Unlike traditional designs that need metal bearings or screws, this relies entirely on its 3D-printed structure and solid infill to self-right. Accessible Printing (NO AMS Needed): A smart multipart design lets you print different colors on separate plates for a multi-color look. A rapid single-color version is also included. Streamlined Assembly: Intuitive tolerances allow pieces to fit together smoothly, requiring only a small drop of adhesive for a highly durable bond. 🛠️ Step-by-Step Assembly Guide The assembly process is straightforward and consists of 6 simple steps . For the best results, having some CA glue (superglue) on hand is recommended. Step 1: Clean the Prints Carefully remove all support material from the printed parts. Ensure all mating surfaces are clean and smooth for a flush fit. Step 2: Install the Base Connectors Insert all four alignment connectors into the base. Because this model is subject to constant kinetic movement, it is highly recommended to apply a small amount of CA glue in a cross-shape between the connectors to lock them securely. Step 3: Secure the Body Align both components of the body and press the pieces firmly together, holding them in place until the glue has fully set. Step 4: Assemble the Face Details Insert the two eyes into the designated slots on the white belly piece . This may require some force, as they are designed to stay in place without using glue. Step 5: Fit the Belly Panel Press the completed belly and eye assembly directly into the front cutout of the penguin's body. This part is designed for a precise friction-fit and does not require any extra glue . Step 6: Attach the Beak For the final step, add a small drop of glue to the back of the penguin's beak and push it into the face cutout. description: 大家好！此模型是來自 IDW 《Transformers / Back to the Future》 聯名漫畫裡可變成滑板的變形金剛 Skilz ，因為官方一直沒有推出能搭配時光車 Gigawatt 比例的實體玩具，於是自己嘗試建模設計了一款。由於這只是個人設計的業餘作品，可能沒辦法像官方玩具那麼完善，但基本的變形功能以及可動關節都有做出來，分享給同樣喜歡這個角色的朋友！ 模型是採用單色列印，後續再上色的模式，因為零件細小，用AMS分色列印效果可能不佳。 模型基本設計： 【嘗試完全變形】：設計上可從機器人模式變形為滑板模式，不需要拆卸零件，但也可拆下部分零件做為原創武器，讓整體比例更協調。 【配合 Gigawatt 比例】：機器人模式的尺寸是有特別與官方的時光車 Gigawatt 進行調整，放在一起的比例感還算合適。 【可動關節與支架】：模型具備基本的可動關節可調整姿勢，背後也附上直徑3mm的插孔安裝通用支架，可有不同的展示方式。 ⚠️ 一些列印與組裝的提醒： 【0.2噴嘴與0.4噴嘴】：使用0.2噴嘴搭配0.06層高可達到最佳列印品質，若使用0.4噴嘴則需搭配0.08層高，但零件可能出現小瑕疵需要額外修整。 【線材與底板清潔】：建議使用已烘乾的PLA進行列印，列印前適當清潔底板確保過程中零件不位移。 【分盤列印】：因為零件數量不少且細小，因此把零件做成框架的模式進行列印。建議按照檔案內的安排分盤列印，確保較高的成功率與品質。 【細節與公差】：零件尺寸較小，列印後關節處或插銷插孔的位置可能需要自行修剪，或是用筆刀微調才能更順利組裝與變形。 【支撐與底板接觸面】：在拆除支撐時須注意有完整拆除，若有殘留可能會影響組裝，會有過緊甚至是損壞零件的可能。零件與底板接觸面的部分需注意是否有毛邊，這部分也可能會影響組裝。 【懸空處修整】：部分懸空處可不用加上支撐，但需要處理垂下的耗材，避免影響組裝。 各框架列印完成冷卻後，可直接由此處提起，把零件從底板上一次分離。 以下是詳細的組裝步驟： 1. 身體部分以側向90度的方向插入後再轉正即可，若過緊可能是球關節上有毛邊需稍微修整。 2. 大腿部分直接按壓裝入即可，可放在桌面上施力會比較輕鬆。須注意左右零件不同。 3. 小腿安裝左右腿對稱，零件插槽可先安裝測試完鬆緊度再把C扣扣上。 4. 肩關節可由約45度角的方向壓入，安裝上臂時請小心肩關節滑動，上臂零件可放在桌面上再壓入會比較容易施力。 5. 手臂C扣較脆弱，安裝前須注意零件狀態是否需要修整。 6. 頭部以側向90度方向插入，再轉正即可。 7. 背後插孔部分若無支撐，可能會有一些懸垂的耗材需要移除。小翅膀轉軸上有支撐需要移除，請確保有確實移除乾淨，不然可能會損壞背後的卡槽。安裝時建議由側向卡入後再進行旋轉，第一次旋轉時須注意不要讓轉軸滑出卡槽。 8. 腳部的第一次變形，由於零件細小，在把零件從插槽拔出時須注意力道，可藉由旋轉腳掌零件讓收納過程不會有零件干涉。完成後腳掌零件與小腿間有卡扣可固定。 這算是一個還在實驗與優化階段的嘗試，稱不上是非常成熟的模型。大家如果有任何修改建議， 非常歡迎在下方留言討論 ，謝謝大家！

description: Anime Statue Series — Broly Ultra-Real Statue 1. Design Concept Following the cosmic dominance of Frieza, the series now unleashes the absolute pinnacle of unbridled destruction— The Legendary Super Saiyan: Broly . This sculpture reinterprets Broly as a hyper-real, high-impact anime statue, focusing on sheer presence, terrifying silhouette, and immense physical mass. Eschewing mechanical or robotic elements, this piece is intentionally built with exaggerated organic tension, delivering surreal realism through raw, compressed biological power. Instead of hard geometric patterns, the curves flow like a high-density torrent of muscle, layered to evoke a sense of immense internal energy pressure rippling beneath the surface. The design amplifies Broly’s iconic massive torso, towering trapezius, and heavy, grounded battle stance. With fists clenched in boiling rage, broad shoulders tensed, and his face lowered with a ruthless, erratic glare, the statue perfectly balances nostalgia, overwhelming menace, and chaotic energy. This work is sculpted for collectors who value volume, mood, expression, and absolute centerpiece impact. 2. Engineering & Printability The statue is engineered for maximum stability in large-scale FDM printing, optimized as a monolithic, one-shot statue rather than an articulated or multi-part kit: Center of Gravity & Base Adhesion: The structural volume beneath his iconic waist cloth has been redistributed to act as a solid ballast pillar. This enhances bed adhesion and center-of-gravity compensation, ensuring tall prints remain secure throughout the entire process. Reinforced Geometry: The sprawling spikes of his hair and accessory tips feature reinforced cross-sections, drastically reducing the risk of fragile tip-break failures due to printer vibrations. Volumetric Readability: At a 0.2 mm layer height, the hyper-defined muscle swells translate naturally into deep shadow transitions under directional light. The geometry minimizes extreme overhang risks while maintaining clean contours, making it a joy for hobbyists preparing for sanding, priming, and painting. 3. Display & Customization This piece thrives in apocalyptic, wasteland, or shattered-world display settings. It pairs beautifully with barren environments—cracked earth, industrial decay, or smoking crater backdrops—giving Broly the aura of a living bio-weapon dropped into a ruined dimension. For finishing, artists can push the limits with advanced techniques: heavy dark-void shading in the muscle crevices, airbrushed green energy reflections (OSL) across his flesh, or incandescent accents highlighting his veins. Under directional studio lighting, the aggressive silhouette casts double-density shadows that make his biological frame feel as dense and impenetrable as forged armor. 4. Conclusion The Hyper-Real Broly statue stands as a core collectible showcase piece for print collectors who adore catastrophic charm and stylized plausibility. It is physical, present, and narratively thunderous—proving that high collectible impact isn't born from moving parts, but from unfiltered sculptural presence. It transforms childhood awe into tangible power, blending weight, menace, and surreal realism into one definitive centerpiece that dominates the space it commands. Quick Tips: Avoid photography/timelapse mode for tall, complex prints to minimize print failure risks. Calibrate your machine and use dry, stable filament for the best surface quality—Bambu gray remains my absolute go-to. Needle-nose pliers combined with Bambu’s FAC002-N scraper make post-print support cleanup incredibly efficient.
